Description: This is a voluntary ex-ante transparency (VEAT) notice. It acknowledges that University College Cork (UCC) contracted with Universidad de Málaga (UMA), for the provision of support in Scientific Advisory, online learning resource enhancement, and online & in-person training for the Copernicus Atmospheric Monitoring Service and Copernicus Climate Change Service, under the competitively won ECMWF Service Contract CJS2_156b_UCC. Under CJS2_156b_UCC, UCC is leading a Service team to provide support to the ECMWF in implementing training events and online learning resources for the two Copernicus Services. UMA will contribute to the Scientific Advisory Committee, online learning resource, and training event activities for the overall Service contract, providing niche technical, expertise and scientific oversight support. UMA were uniquely placed in terms of skillsets, professional networks and relationships to perform their role in this overall service contract, further enhanced by their good standing, and track record of excellence. They brought the international European Topic Centre for Spatial Analysis and Synthesis (ETC-UMA) into the Service Contract, where environmental knowledge to support evidence-based policy and decision-making at different scales is developed, supported by the work of the Khaos research group, specialised in Big Data analytics, machine learning and artificial intelligence - all of which are quickly growing topics of interest to Copernicus trainees. The ETC-UMA team have thematic skills and perspectives of high importance to the training topics the Service is expected to advise on, including environmental remote sensing, geospatial data management and publication, indicator development, ecosystems and services assessments of marine and terrestrial environments. Additionally, researchers at ETC-UMA are currently part of the core team of the European Topic Centre on Data Integration and Digitalisation (ETC/DI) supporting the Copernicus Land Monitoring Service. UMA leads on their user uptake initiatives to promote the service portfolio within the European Environment Agency, among the other ETCs and Commission Services (such as DG Agri, Eurostat, etc.), and supports stakeholder engagement at Member State level through preparing capacity building material and workshop design. As a university, UMA is a key contributor of training experience, enhanced by organising Copernicus Hackathons, their connections within the Copernicus community, and their founding role in the Copernicus Academy. As such, they bring the skills, expertise, networks, good standing and track record to meet the needs of the Service's Scientific Advisory Committee, Training Event implementation, and Online training resource development. This is in close alignment with the requirements of the overarching Service contract between UCC and the ECMWF, specifically to deliver high-quality, customised training and developing learning resources for Copernicus services that are quality controlled to a standard of high scientific rigour. The institute was therefore selected to participate in the bid for the CJS2_156b ITT as their unique combination of skillsets, technical expertise, capabilities and networks complemented those of the bidding consortium, completing it’s offering to the ECMWF. They were integral to the awarded bid, and have been contracted accordingly.

procedureTitle: Provision of Distributed Antenna System for Haymarket
description: The NTA is seeking tender responses from Service Providers who have proven skills, knowledge and experience to install a Distributed Antenna System (DAS) for its Haymarket office located at Haymarket House, Smithfield, Dublin 7. The DAS system installed must be able to support and facilitate signal re-broadcasting of mobile network operators throughout the building. The Service Provider will provide the following services (the “Services”). i. The design and installation of a DAS solution suitable for the NTAs mobile requirements on site in Smithfield, capable of delivery of the below minimum reception standards: o 800 MHz band o 900 MHz band (3G – Voice – will be live on the system) o 1800 MHz band (4G – Data – will be live on this system) o 2100 MHz band (3G – Voice - will be live on this system) o 2600 MHz band ii. Presenting design criteria to secure approval for technical sign-off from the MNOs and NTA prior to installation. The Service Provider will be responsible for ensuring that all services are completed in line with building fit out schedule, currently planned for Q2 2024. This is an indicative timeline. The DAS will be installed to ensure seamless mobile phone connectivity throughout the entire building. The system must be fully compliant with the latest JOTS and MIPS.

Under CJS2_156b_UCC, UCC is leading a Service team to provide support to the ECMWF in implementing training events and online learning resources for the two Copernicus Services. CLS will (i) support the online learning resource activities for the overall Service contract, providing technical support to implement resource solutions, (ii) contribute to the Scientific Advisory Committee, and (iii) support Training event implementation. CLS were uniquely placed in terms of skillsets, professional networks and relationships to perform their role in this overall service contract, further enhanced by their good standing, and track record of excellence. They have extensive experience in developing integrated offers to a broad range of Service-relevant stakeholders including: government, industry and the scientific community and services, in sectors such as Environment & climate monitoring, Mobility, Energy & infrastructures, amongst others. They have a dedicated team of data scientists who work closely with oceanographers to develop new methodologies, understandings and ocean science communications. They have coupled this with a growing, and impressive training portfolio in Earth Observation applications - critical to the Copernicus programme – and are existing suppliers of data and training materials to the Copernicus Climate Service, and Copernicus Marine Service (in addition to ESA, CNES and many other global partners, which brought considerable potential for synergies to the Service). CLS have also delivered staff training programmes to field and IT operators and end-users, while having also developed a full Moodle course for EUMETSAT, and a range of Jupyter applications and notebooks, the bedrock of the ECMWF's online training offering. Their staff are experienced in delivering in-person training on ocean scient topics such as altimetry, a key area for capacity building in the Copernicus community. In addition, they bring their oceans experience, training experience and knowledge of satellite systems to satisfy a critical niche for expertise in the Service’s Scientific Advisory Committee - a key Quality Control mechanism embedded within the contract Service. This is in close alignment with the requirements of the overarching Service contract between UCC and the ECMWF, specifically to deliver high-quality, customised training and developing learning resources for Copernicus services that are quality controlled to a standard of high scientific rigour. The company was therefore selected to participate in the bid for the CJS2_156b ITT as their unique combination of skillsets, technical expertise, capabilities and networks complemented those of the bidding consortium, completing it’s offering to the ECMWF. They were integral to the awarded bid, and have been contracted accordingly.

Description: This is a voluntary ex-ante transparency (VEAT) notice. For example, the department is the initiator and coordinator of the Erasmus Mundus Joint Master "Copernicus Master in Digital Earth", and they are co-founders of the Copernicus Academy, fostering the emergence of regional and virtual Copernicus hubs. Within the Erasmus Skills Alliance project EO4GEO (2018-2022), they acted as Academic Coordinator to push the Copernicus downstream sector. Additionally, they have engaged in the downstream service evolution for 15+ years in various application areas of interest to the Copernicus community, including biodiversity monitoring, disaster response, and climate change adaptation. This, in addition to their academic portfolio, uniquely places them to contribute to the Service's Scientific Advisory Committee - a key Quality Control mechanism embedded within the contract Service – while equipping the Service with their highly beneficial professional networks and Copernicus experience. This is in close alignment with the requirements of the overarching Service contract between UCC and the ECMWF, specifically to deliver high-quality, customised training and developing learning resources for Copernicus services that are quality controlled to a standard of high scientific rigour. The company was therefore selected to participate in the bid for the CJS2_156b ITT as their unique combination of skillsets, technical expertise, capabilities and networks complemented those of the bidding consortium, completing it’s offering to the ECMWF. They were integral to the awarded bid, and have been contracted accordingly.

description: Offshore Geotechnical Surveys
lotDescription: The Contracting Entity intends to establish a Qualification System to procure the scope of services pertaining to offshore geotechnical surveys for the development of its offshore wind farm (OWF) project(s) in Ireland and the UK. The scope of services pertaining to the geotechnical surveys are intended to provide sufficient geotechnical data to allow the characterisation of the sub-seabed strata in order to refine a three-dimensional soils model of the offshore windfarm site. These details will be used to initiate the design of the WTG and sub-station foundations and to carry out a comprehensive analysis of the installation methodology. The output from the survey will directly support the subsequent Front-End Engineering & Design (FEED) activities for the OWF site. The qualification system may include projects developed by ESB, ESB Joint Venture companies (existing or yet to be formed), ESB subsidiary companies or companies ESB Group has a minority interest in. A qualification System Questionnaire setting out the requirements for qualification and information on the qualification process is available to download at : https://www.etenders.gov.ie/epps/dps/prepareViewCfTDPSWS.do?resourceId=3591629

The proposed GNSS field systems should consist of all its necessary components such as antenna, controller, receiver batteries etc. and should be supplied with a rugged carrying case designed to protect the equipment during transportation and when not in use. The equipment should also be as compact and user friendly as possible to assist the Surveyor in performing their duties for prolonged periods without access to their vehicle.

Environmental Noise Directive. The Environmental Noise Regulations 2018 (S.I No. 549 of 2018) , (and prior to that the Noise Regulations 2006) transpose EU Directive 2002/49/EC relating to the assessment and management of environmental noise, more commonly known as the Environmental Noise Directive (END). This Directive aims to provide a common framework to avoid, prevent or reduce, on a prioritised basis, the harmful effects of exposure to environmental noise. It sets out a two-stage process for addressing environmental noise by requiring Member States to: • Establish the extent of the noise environment by preparing ‘strategic noise maps’ for major roads, railways, airports and agglomerations. • Based on the results of these maps, the competent authorities in each Member State is required to develop action plans to reduce the level of noise where necessary and to maintain environmental noise quality where it is good. The first 5-year noise mapping process covered the period from 2004-2008. The third (2014-18) and fourth cycles (2019-2024) addressed noise from major sources over a specified thresholds as follows: • Agglomeration with 100,000 or more inhabitants: • Major Roads which exceed 3 million vehicles per year • Major Railways with 30,000 or more train passages per year, and, • Major Airports with 50,000 or more movements per year (no change from the first cycle) The fourth cycle has now almost been completed, and preparatory work for the fifth cycle (2025-2028) will be commencing during 2025. The fifth cycle (called Round 5) will also need to incorporate the CNOSSOS-EU (common noise methodologies) as was carried out for the Round 4 cycle of mapping. • For background, the Round 4 Strategic Noise Maps are available on EPA Maps under 'Environment and Wellbeing' and 'Noise' • Some explanatory information can be viewed at: Description: The ‘Environmental Monitoring and Surveillance unit’ within the EPA Office of Radiation Protection and Environmental Monitoring (ORM) is responsible for overseeing the strategic noise mapping process required under the Environmental Noise Directive. The Environmental Noise Regulations 2018 (S.I No. 549 of 2018) , (and prior to that the Noise Regulations 2006) transpose EU Directive 2002/49/EC relating to the assessment and management of environmental noise, more commonly known as the Environmental Noise Directive (END). This Directive aims to provide a common framework to avoid, prevent or reduce, on a prioritised basis, the harmful effects of exposure to environmental noise. It sets out a two-stage process for addressing environmental noise by requiring Member States to: • Establish the extent of the noise environment by preparing ‘strategic noise maps’ for major roads, railways, airports and agglomerations. • Based on the results of these maps, the competent authorities in each Member State is required to develop action plans to reduce the level of noise where necessary and to maintain environmental noise quality where it is good. The first 5-year noise mapping process covered the period from 2004-2008. The third (2014-18) and fourth cycles (2019-2024) addressed noise from major sources over a specified thresholds as follows: • Agglomeration with 100,000 or more inhabitants: • Major Roads which exceed 3 million vehicles per year • Major Railways with 30,000 or more train passages per year, and, • Major Airports with 50,000 or more movements per year (no change from the first cycle) The fourth cycle has now almost been completed, and preparatory work for the fifth cycle (2025-2028) will be commencing during 2025. The fifth cycle (called Round 5) will also need to incorporate the CNOSSOS-EU (common noise methodologies) as was carried out for the Round 4 cycle of mapping. • For background, the Round 4 Strategic Noise Maps are available on EPA Maps under 'Environment and Wellbeing' and 'Noise' • Some explanatory information can be viewed at: https://www.epa.ie/our-services/monitoring--assessment/noise/noise-mapping-and-action-plans/

Description: Met Éireann, Ireland’s National Meteorological Service, looks to upgrade its satellite observation handling system to ensure continuity of data supply, capacity for higher data rates and new data types from next-generation meteorological satellites over the next 10 years, and to increase the resilience and geo-redundancy of this data source. The supplier of the new satellite system would be required to provide and install required reception and processing hardware and software, commission and test the system and provide a service and maintenance plan.

procedureTitle: Electrical Works to Scoil Mhuire Coolcotts Co. Wexford

Procedure title: 2424 - Provision of Asset Tracking License and Support
Description: This is a call to competition by AN POST for Provision of Support and Licence for Existing Asset Trackers (the “Contract”). To optimise asset management, An Post require a customer platform which should compile, store and manage data captured from these trackers in a centralised database and software system. This platform should enable real-time visibility and insights for improved asset management. The Contract, the subject of this competition is a Contract for 5 years with an option for one or more extensions by up to 3 years, at AN POST’s discretion, up to a maximum duration of 8 years subject to the terms and conditions of the Contract.

Due to the extended duration of the pandemic, the changing patient care pathway and the ongoing need to support a post pandemic covid vaccination regime, continued integration and expansion to meet Public Health requirements was necessary. The solution has undergone significant development over three years, evolving from a minimum viable product into a comprehensive immunisation system capable of managing multiple vaccine types. A network of interconnected software applications, data repositories, integration points, platforms and services have been built up to create a complex and mature Immunisation Ecosystem with Covax at its core. The capability to extend Covax to meet the requirements for other immunisation programmes, such as Flu and Pneumococcal, has already been delivered and proven. Covax is now an embedded component of the national IT infrastructure used to record Covid, Influenza (Flu), and Pneumococcal vaccinations. It is currently the largest patient database in the HSE, with 4.4 million patient records and over 16 million recorded vaccinations. The HSE now intends to progress with the addition of further vaccinations leading to Covax becoming the National Immunisation Information System (NIIS). description: In December 2020, the HSE procured a solution under Emergency Procurement Regulation 32 to support the response to the Covid 19 Immunisation programme. The solution was built on Salesforce CRM platform and provided an immunisation system (Covax) and a public facing support platform (Service Cloud). Due to the extended duration of the pandemic, the ongoing need for comprehensive vaccination management, and a changing patient care pathway, continued integration and expansion of the solution was required to meet Public Health requirements. Covax has undergone significant development over three years, evolving from a MVP into a comprehensive immunisation system capable of managing multiple vaccine types. Covax vaccination platform has evolved to support the following: patient account creation; vaccination recording; full patient vaccination histories; administration of multiple vaccine products; configurable interval times and doses; configurable risk factors; product-based eligibility criteria; adverse reaction capabilities; diverse vaccine administration locations. Additional functionality includes patient portal; appointment scheduling; reporting and analytics; user training platform; support platform; communication platform. With Covax embedded as the core, a network of interconnected software applications, data repositories, integration points, platforms and services have been built up to create the comprehensive and mature national immunisation ecosystem which is in use today. Vaccination records are ingested into Covax from GPs, Pharmacies, and various Community organisations. Data is enriched on Covax through integration with IHI, GP registry, Eircode, and a vaccination asset management system. National vaccination reporting is enabled though integration with the HSE’s data lake. Covax is an established and embedded cornerstone of the national IT infrastructure. It is currently the largest patient database in the HSE, with over 4.4 million patient records and over 16 million recorded vaccinations. The architecture of the Covax system is proven in terms of both performance and scale, with the recording of 400,000 vaccinations per week at peak. The Covax public-facing portal has facilitated the self-registration of 2.2 million patients for vaccination to date and appointment scheduling functionality has created over 7.5 million appointments. Since 2021, Covax has ingested over 6 million vaccination records from GPs and 2 million from pharmacies. To date, over 20,000 clinical and operational staff have been trained to use the Covax system. Embedded in the pandemic response was the requirement for HSE Live to provide public-facing support. Salesforce Service Cloud was used to provide this support, and with extensive and incremental development, this generic platform was tailored for use by multiple Covid support teams across the HSE including HSE Live, DCC team, HSE NSD (National Service Desk), Covax support and GP Resolver teams.

Description: In December 2020, the HSE procured a solution under Emergency Procurement Regulation 32 to support the response to the Covid 19 Immunisation programme. The solution was built on Salesforce CRM platform and provided an immunisation system (Covax) and a public facing support platform (Service Cloud). Due to the extended duration of the pandemic, the ongoing need for comprehensive vaccination management, and a changing patient care pathway, continued integration and expansion of the solution was required to meet Public Health requirements. Covax has undergone significant development over three years, evolving from a MVP into a comprehensive immunisation system capable of managing multiple vaccine types. Covax vaccination platform has evolved to support the following: patient account creation; vaccination recording; full patient vaccination histories; administration of multiple vaccine products; configurable interval times and doses; configurable risk factors; product-based eligibility criteria; adverse reaction capabilities; diverse vaccine administration locations. Additional functionality includes patient portal; appointment scheduling; reporting and analytics; user training platform; support platform; communication platform. With Covax embedded as the core, a network of interconnected software applications, data repositories, integration points, platforms and services have been built up to create the comprehensive and mature national immunisation ecosystem which is in use today. Vaccination records are ingested into Covax from GPs, Pharmacies, and various Community organisations. Data is enriched on Covax through integration with IHI, GP registry, Eircode, and a vaccination asset management system. National vaccination reporting is enabled though integration with the HSE’s data lake. Covax is an established and embedded cornerstone of the national IT infrastructure. It is currently the largest patient database in the HSE, with over 4.4 million patient records and over 16 million recorded vaccinations. The architecture of the Covax system is proven in terms of both performance and scale, with the recording of 400,000 vaccinations per week at peak. The Covax public-facing portal has facilitated the self-registration of 2.2 million patients for vaccination to date and appointment scheduling functionality has created over 7.5 million appointments. Since 2021, Covax has ingested over 6 million vaccination records from GPs and 2 million from pharmacies. To date, over 20,000 clinical and operational staff have been trained to use the Covax system. Embedded in the pandemic response was the requirement for HSE Live to provide public-facing support. Salesforce Service Cloud was used to provide this support, and with extensive and incremental development, this generic platform was tailored for use by multiple Covid support teams across the HSE including HSE Live, DCC team, HSE NSD (National Service Desk), Covax support and GP Resolver teams.

Procedure title: Upgrade of Met Éireann's Satellite Observation Handling System
Description: Met Éireann, Ireland’s National Meteorological Service, looks to upgrade its satellite observation handling system to ensure continuity of data supply, capacity for higher data rates and new data types from next-generation meteorological satellites over the next 10 years, and to increase the resilience and geo-redundancy of this data source. The supplier of the new satellite system would be required to provide and install required reception and processing hardware and software, commission and test the system and provide a service and maintenance plan.

Environmental Noise Directive. The Environmental Noise Regulations 2018 (S.I No. 549 of 2018) , (and prior to that the Noise Regulations 2006) transpose EU Directive 2002/49/EC relating to the assessment and management of environmental noise, more commonly known as the Environmental Noise Directive (END). This Directive aims to provide a common framework to avoid, prevent or reduce, on a prioritised basis, the harmful effects of exposure to environmental noise. It sets out a two-stage process for addressing environmental noise by requiring Member States to: • Establish the extent of the noise environment by preparing ‘strategic noise maps’ for major roads, railways, airports and agglomerations. • Based on the results of these maps, the competent authorities in each Member State is required to develop action plans to reduce the level of noise where necessary and to maintain environmental noise quality where it is good. The first 5-year noise mapping process covered the period from 2004-2008. The third (2014-18) and fourth cycles (2019-2024) addressed noise from major sources over a specified thresholds as follows: • Agglomeration with 100,000 or more inhabitants: • Major Roads which exceed 3 million vehicles per year • Major Railways with 30,000 or more train passages per year, and, • Major Airports with 50,000 or more movements per year (no change from the first cycle) The fourth cycle has now almost been completed, and preparatory work for the fifth cycle (2025-2028) will be commencing during 2025. The fifth cycle (called Round 5) will also need to incorporate the CNOSSOS-EU (common noise methodologies) as was carried out for the Round 4 cycle of mapping. • For background, the Round 4 Strategic Noise Maps are available on EPA Maps under 'Environment and Wellbeing' and 'Noise' • Some explanatory information can be viewed at: Description: The ‘Environmental Monitoring and Surveillance unit’ within the EPA Office of Radiation Protection and Environmental Monitoring (ORM) is responsible for overseeing the strategic noise mapping process required under the Environmental Noise Directive. The Environmental Noise Regulations 2018 (S.I No. 549 of 2018) , (and prior to that the Noise Regulations 2006) transpose EU Directive 2002/49/EC relating to the assessment and management of environmental noise, more commonly known as the Environmental Noise Directive (END). This Directive aims to provide a common framework to avoid, prevent or reduce, on a prioritised basis, the harmful effects of exposure to environmental noise. It sets out a two-stage process for addressing environmental noise by requiring Member States to: • Establish the extent of the noise environment by preparing ‘strategic noise maps’ for major roads, railways, airports and agglomerations. • Based on the results of these maps, the competent authorities in each Member State is required to develop action plans to reduce the level of noise where necessary and to maintain environmental noise quality where it is good. The first 5-year noise mapping process covered the period from 2004-2008. The third (2014-18) and fourth cycles (2019-2024) addressed noise from major sources over a specified thresholds as follows: • Agglomeration with 100,000 or more inhabitants: • Major Roads which exceed 3 million vehicles per year • Major Railways with 30,000 or more train passages per year, and, • Major Airports with 50,000 or more movements per year (no change from the first cycle) The fourth cycle has now almost been completed, and preparatory work for the fifth cycle (2025-2028) will be commencing during 2025. The fifth cycle (called Round 5) will also need to incorporate the CNOSSOS-EU (common noise methodologies) as was carried out for the Round 4 cycle of mapping. • For background, the Round 4 Strategic Noise Maps are available on EPA Maps under 'Environment and Wellbeing' and 'Noise' • Some explanatory information can be viewed at: https://www.epa.ie/our-services/monitoring--assessment/noise/noise-mapping-and-action-plans/

The proposed robotic total station solutions should consist of all its necessary components such as a lightweight detail pole, bipod for telescopic pole, tripod for total station, clamps, Li-On batteries, power cables, bags etc. and should be supplied with a rugged carrying case designed to protect the equipment during transportation and when not in use. description: This Dynamic Purchasing System for Plant Hire has been transitioned to the new eTenders platform https://www.etenders.gov.ie with the Resource ID 4211102. Additionally, the following updates to the Request for Tender (RFT) process have also been incorporated and will take effect no earlier than the 7th October 2024: • Lot 1 Contract Award Criteria has been amended from 100% Total Cost to facilitate inclusion of Price/Quality where Price may range from 60% - 100%, and Quality may range from 0% - 40%. • Lot 2 Contract Award Criteria has been amended from 90% Total Cost and 10% Project Methodology to facilitate inclusion of Price/Quality, where Price may range from 60% - 100%, and Quality may range from 0% - 40%. • Lot 3 Contract Award Criteria has been amended from 90% Total Cost and 10% Project Methodology to facilitate inclusion of Price/Quality, where Price may range from 60% - 100%, and Quality may range from 0% - 40%. • Inclusion of the Public Works Term Maintenance and Refurbishment Contract (TMRC) (PW-CF11) in Lot 3 as a Contract option. • Inclusion of the option to establish a substitution list for a Request for Tender (RFT) under Lot 3 when executed using the Public Works Term Maintenance and Refurbishment Contract (TMRC) (PW-CF11). Updated Tender Documents are available for downloading from https://www.etenders.gov.ie by selecting the “DPS Documents” option from the “Show DPS Menu” under Resource ID 4211102. See Section 5.0, Appendix 4 (Lot 1), Appendix 5 (Lot 2), Appendix 6 (Lot 3) of the Instructions Document, and the Plant Hire DPS - Terms & Conditions - Lot 3. The application process to join the Dynamic Purchasing System for Plant Hire remains on https://www.supplygov.ie

Title: Ireland – Hire of agricultural machinery with operator – Dynamic Purchasing System for Plant Hire
Procedure title: Dynamic Purchasing System for Plant Hire
Description: This Dynamic Purchasing System for Plant Hire has been transitioned to the new eTenders platform https://www.etenders.gov.ie with the Resource ID 4211102. Additionally, the following updates to the Request for Tender (RFT) process have also been incorporated and will take effect no earlier than the 7th October 2024: • Lot 1 Contract Award Criteria has been amended from 100% Total Cost to facilitate inclusion of Price/Quality where Price may range from 60% - 100%, and Quality may range from 0% - 40%. • Lot 2 Contract Award Criteria has been amended from 90% Total Cost and 10% Project Methodology to facilitate inclusion of Price/Quality, where Price may range from 60% - 100%, and Quality may range from 0% - 40%. • Lot 3 Contract Award Criteria has been amended from 90% Total Cost and 10% Project Methodology to facilitate inclusion of Price/Quality, where Price may range from 60% - 100%, and Quality may range from 0% - 40%. • Inclusion of the Public Works Term Maintenance and Refurbishment Contract (TMRC) (PW-CF11) in Lot 3 as a Contract option. • Inclusion of the option to establish a substitution list for a Request for Tender (RFT) under Lot 3 when executed using the Public Works Term Maintenance and Refurbishment Contract (TMRC) (PW-CF11). Updated Tender Documents are available for downloading from https://www.etenders.gov.ie by selecting the “DPS Documents” option from the “Show DPS Menu” under Resource ID 4211102. See Section 5.0, Appendix 4 (Lot 1), Appendix 5 (Lot 2), Appendix 6 (Lot 3) of the Instructions Document, and the Plant Hire DPS - Terms & Conditions - Lot 3. The application process to join the Dynamic Purchasing System for Plant Hire remains on https://www.supplygov.ie

Title: Ireland – Global navigation and positioning systems (GPS or equivalent) – Supply of Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) Field Equipment for Tailte Éireann
Procedure title: Supply of Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) Field Equipment for Tailte Éireann
Description: Supply of Geodetic Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) enabled rover stations, which will form part of our field surveying workflows. The proposed GNSS field systems should consist of all its necessary components such as antenna, controller, receiver batteries etc. and should be supplied with a rugged carrying case designed to protect the equipment during transportation and when not in use. The equipment should also be as compact and user friendly as possible to assist the Surveyor in performing their duties for prolonged periods without access to their vehicle.
Lot description: Supply of Geodetic Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) enabled rover stations, which will form part of our field surveying workflows. The proposed GNSS field systems should consist of all its necessary components such as antenna, controller, receiver batteries etc. and should be supplied with a rugged carrying case designed to protect the equipment during transportation and when not in use. The equipment should also be as compact and user friendly as possible to assist the Surveyor in performing their duties for prolonged periods without access to their vehicle.

description: Met Eireann is invites tenders for supporting the monitoring of the Green House Gas-Nitrous Oxide, at its environmental monitoring site at Bray Head Valentia Island for a Proof Of Concept phase. The tenderer must be able to deploy Instrumentation in an ICOS (Integrated Carbon Observing System) compliant fashion with respect to calibration and data analysis, for the duration of the POC. The tenderer must be able to provide specialist expertise to utilise the data from the system to provide the basis for comprehensive modelling and analysis approaches to allows for the generation of a ‘top down’ estimate of national greenhouse gas emissions of the gas. The tenderer must also provide training to local staff to ensure appropriate skills and knowledge transfer and to also produce an end of POC report.
lotDescription: Met Eireann is invites tenders for supporting the monitoring of the Green House Gas-Nitrous Oxide, at its environmental monitoring site at Bray Head Valentia Island for a Proof Of Concept phase. The tenderer must be able to deploy Instrumentation in an ICOS (Integrated Carbon Observing System) compliant fashion with respect to calibration and data analysis, for the duration of the POC. Procedure title: Maintenance and Servicing of existing Fire Detection Alarm and Emergency Lighting Systems
Description: The Muiriosa Foundation is undertaking a call for tender for the maintenance and servicing of our existing fore detection fire alarm and emergency lighting systems. Maintenance and servicing is required in numerous different locations in Laois, Offaly, Tipperary, Kildare, Meath, Westmeath and Longford as per appendix 6, 7, 8 and these lists may vary from time to time. This tender also includes installation of new fire detection alarm and emercency lighting systemsin Muiriosa Foundation owned properties when required.
Lot description: The Muiriosa Foundation is undertaking a call for tender for the maintenance and servicing of our existing fore detection fire alarm and emergency lighting systems. Maintenance and servicing is required in numerous different locations in Laois, Offaly, Tipperary, Kildare, Meath, Westmeath and Longford as per appendix 6, 7, 8 and these lists may vary from time to time. This tender also includes installation of new fire detection alarm and emercency lighting systemsin Muiriosa Foundation owned properties when required.

The Environmental Noise Regulations 2018 (S.I No. 549 of 2018) , (and prior to that the Noise Regulations 2006) transpose EU Directive 2002/49/EC relating to the assessment and management of environmental noise, more commonly known as the Environmental Noise Directive (END). This Directive aims to provide a common framework to avoid, prevent or reduce, on a prioritised basis, the harmful effects of exposure to environmental noise. It sets out a two-stage process for addressing environmental noise by requiring Member States to: • Establish the extent of the noise environment by preparing ‘strategic noise maps’ for major roads, railways, airports and agglomerations. • Based on the results of these maps, the competent authorities in each Member State is required to develop action plans to reduce the level of noise where necessary and to maintain environmental noise quality where it is good. The first 5-year noise mapping process covered the period from 2004-2008. The third (2014-18) and fourth cycles (2019-2024) addressed noise from major sources over a specified thresholds as follows: • Agglomeration with 100,000 or more inhabitants: • Major Roads which exceed 3 million vehicles per year • Major Railways with 30,000 or more train passages per year, and, • Major Airports with 50,000 or more movements per year (no change from the first cycle) The fourth cycle has now almost been completed, and preparatory work for the fifth cycle (2025-2028) will be commencing during 2025. The fifth cycle (called Round 5) will also need to incorporate the CNOSSOS-EU (common noise methodologies) as was carried out for the Round 4 cycle of mapping. • For background, the Round 4 Strategic Noise Maps are available on EPA Maps under 'Environment and Wellbeing' and 'Noise' • Some explanatory information can be viewed at: https://www.epa.ie/our-services/monitoring--assessment/noise/noise-mapping-and-action-plans/

Description: The ‘Environmental Monitoring and Surveillance unit’ within the EPA Office of Radiation Protection and Environmental Monitoring (ORM) is responsible for overseeing the strategic noise mapping process required under the Environmental Noise Directive. The Environmental Noise Regulations 2018 (S.I No. 549 of 2018) , (and prior to that the Noise Regulations 2006) transpose EU Directive 2002/49/EC relating to the assessment and management of environmental noise, more commonly known as the Environmental Noise Directive (END). This Directive aims to provide a common framework to avoid, prevent or reduce, on a prioritised basis, the harmful effects of exposure to environmental noise. It sets out a two-stage process for addressing environmental noise by requiring Member States to: • Establish the extent of the noise environment by preparing ‘strategic noise maps’ for major roads, railways, airports and agglomerations. • Based on the results of these maps, the competent authorities in each Member State is required to develop action plans to reduce the level of noise where necessary and to maintain environmental noise quality where it is good. The first 5-year noise mapping process covered the period from 2004-2008. The third (2014-18) and fourth cycles (2019-2024) addressed noise from major sources over a specified thresholds as follows: • Agglomeration with 100,000 or more inhabitants: • Major Roads which exceed 3 million vehicles per year • Major Railways with 30,000 or more train passages per year, and, • Major Airports with 50,000 or more movements per year (no change from the first cycle) The fourth cycle has now almost been completed, and preparatory work for the fifth cycle (2025-2028) will be commencing during 2025. The fifth cycle (called Round 5) will also need to incorporate the CNOSSOS-EU (common noise methodologies) as was carried out for the Round 4 cycle of mapping. • For background, the Round 4 Strategic Noise Maps are available on EPA Maps under 'Environment and Wellbeing' and 'Noise' • Some explanatory information can be viewed at: https://www.epa.ie/our-services/monitoring--assessment/noise/noise-mapping-and-action-plans/

Title: Ireland – Installation services of meteorological equipment – Upgrade of Met Éireann's Satellite Observation Handling System
Procedure title: Upgrade of Met Éireann's Satellite Observation Handling System
Description: Met Éireann, Ireland’s National Meteorological Service, looks to upgrade its satellite observation handling system. It currently receives satellite meteorology data from the EUMETCast Satellite dissemination service using an antenna-based reception system at its headquarters in Dublin. Met Éireann is also in the process of establishing additional connections to the EUMETCast Terrestrial service at both its headquarters and a second data centre in Dublin, to increase resilience and redundancy in its satellite data supply. The primary aim of this procurement is to upgrade Met Éireann’s satellite observation handling system to ensure continuity of data supply, capacity for higher data rates and new data types from next-generation satellites, and to increase the resilience and geo-redundancy of this important data source. This procurement looks to achieve the following: -Obtain system layout and design guidance for an upgraded satellite reception and processing system; -Procure hardware components to facilitate the reception and processing of current and next-generation meteorological satellite observations by the satellite system. The key hardware components shall include two antenna-dish receivers, six DVB units and required cabling. Complete component requirements will be finalised based on the system design agreed upon with the Contractor; -Procure service for the replacement/installation of required hardware for new system; -Procure the required software for the handling and processing of satellite observations on the reception and processing servers, and the installation of this software; -Procure service to test and commission the new system to receive and process data from EUMETCast dissemination services; -Ensure processed data outputted by the new system is compatible with Met Éireann’s visualisation and assimilation systems; -Procure maintenance and service plan to cover the new system once operational. With an increase in satellite data rates expected within 2024, the capacity of the supplier to perform the replacement of the system within a short time frame will be an important element.

Complete component requirements will be finalised based on the system design agreed upon with the Contractor; -Procure service for the replacement/installation of required hardware for new system; -Procure the required software for the handling and processing of satellite observations on the reception and processing servers, and the installation of this software; -Procure service to test and commission the new system to receive and process data from EUMETCast dissemination services; -Ensure processed data outputted by the new system is compatible with Met Éireann’s visualisation and assimilation systems; -Procure maintenance and service plan to cover the new system once operational. Title: Ireland – Hire of aircraft with crew – Provision of Aircraft and Related Services for Tailte Éireann
Procedure title: Provision of Aircraft and Related Services for Tailte Éireann
Description: Tailte Éireann require the provision of an aerial service comprising two aircrafts and all associated requirements for the operations of our digital mapping sensors. This Request for Tender sets out the requirements for the provision of Aircraft Services capable of carrying Tailte Éireann - Surveying aerial sensors and Tailte Éireann staff and enabling its Remote Sensing Unit to achieve national coverage of imagery, height, and related datasets.
Lot description: Tailte Éireann require the provision of an aerial service comprising two aircrafts and all associated requirements for the operations of our digital mapping sensors. Title: Ireland – IT services: consulting, software development, Internet and support – Mobile Data Collection Platform.
Procedure title: Mobile Data Collection Platform.
Description: Iarnród Éireann (IÉ) is seeking a partner to implement a range of field work management applications with a data collection system at its core. It is planned to implement the system with approximately 500 users, initially. The core system will link to SAP, SharePoint and other IT systems using a-synchronous connections (via API), and will initially be focused on 6 elements: i. Work Order Management Application; ii. Data Collection Tools; iii. Form Creation; iv. Lone Work Systems; v. GIS and GPS Navigation System; vi. Service Level Agreement. IÉ requires that this Mobile Data Collection Platform will be flexible enough to be applied to a number of field data collection business processes in various areas of the organisation.The current contract with AMT Sybex is set to expire on January 22, 2025. At tender stage in 2017 it was considered that a seven-year term would be sufficient as it was anticipated that the mobile data collection functionality would be incorporated into other enterprise-wide systems during the term of the contract, negating the need for a separate standalone platform. However, while it is still intended to incorporate this functionality into a separate enterprise solution (e.g. as part of the proposed SAP upgrade), since this system is core to the IÉ Asset Management System and is also utilised by IÉ Safety Teams across the organisation, continuity of service is required. The integration of Fieldreach into IÉ's operations has been extensive, with the platform being deeply embedded in engineering workflows and asset management activities. Transitioning to a new provider at this stage would introduce significant technical and economic challenges: • Technical Complexity and Integration Costs: The integration of Fieldreach with IÉ’s SAP ECC system and other critical business processes was a highly customized and iterative process. A new provider would necessitate substantial redevelopment and re-integration, leading to high costs and potential disruptions in service. If a new system was to be procured, an alternative integration layer between SAP and the new tool would have to be designed, built and tested. This would require resources from GITT, IÉ technical staff and a third party integration partner. It is anticipated that the costs associated with these works would be in the region of €1M (excl. VAT). Further additional duplication of costs and risk would be incurred by transferring data from the current suppliers’ servers to those of a new supplier. • Operational Disruption: Adopting a new platform would require extensive retraining of approximately 800 users. This transition period could significantly impact productivity and the efficiency of our maintenance and asset management activities, risking compliance and operational integrity. On the basis of the above and based on the substantial technical and economic implications, IÉ is seeking approval to conclude negotiations with AMT Sybex with a view to extending the term of this contract for a further period of up to 5 years up to January 2030, during which, it is anticipated the platform will be phased out as IÉ transitions to another enterprise solution. By extending the contract with AMT Sybex, IÉ can ensure the continuity of critical asset management operations, avoid unnecessary disruptions, and maintain operational efficiency. The continuation of the current platform will facilitate a seamless workflow for our staff and uphold the standards of our asset management processes.

Procedure title: Habitat Mapping and Habitat Condition Assessments of the Rossbehy Spit
Description: 1.3. In summary, the Services comprise: a new habitat mapping and habitat condition assessment surveys of Rossbehy Spit, County Kerry, using existing and/or novel technologies as appropriate. This is to both update and improve our understanding of the occurrence and distribution of the habitats found here. Habitats at this site were last mapped in 2007-2008 during the Saltmarsh Monitoring Project and in 2004-2006 as part of the Coastal Monitoring Project – please see supporting documents for Castlemaine Harbour SAC for details of these studies: https://www.npws.ie/protected-sites/sac/000343

Title: Ireland – IT services: consulting, software development, Internet and support – 2424 - Provision of Asset Tracking License and Support
Procedure title: 2424 - Provision of Asset Tracking License and Support
Description: This is a call to competition by AN POST for Provision of Support and Licence for Existing Asset Trackers (the “Contract”). To optimise asset management, An Post require a customer platform which should compile, store and manage data captured from these trackers in a centralised database and software system. This platform should enable real-time visibility and insights for improved asset management. The Contract, the subject of this competition is a Contract for 5 years with an option for one or more extensions by up to 3 years, at AN POST’s discretion, up to a maximum duration of 8 years subject to the terms and conditions of the Contract.

Description: General Description of the Proposed Contract The Contracting Entity intends to procure material supplies for the provision of FOX615 equipment to expand ESB’s existing FOX615 network as well as a standalone project for the replacement of FOX515 with FOX615 multiplexers. It is also intended to procure support services for the FOX515 replacement program consisting of design, project management and commissioning resources. It is proposed that the Contract will include the following (non-exhaustive list – high level scope): • Provision of FOX615,FOX612 equipment to include full suite of modules available for ongoing projects. • Provision of FOX615,FOX612 equipment to include full suite of modules available for 515 replacement project. • Associated licenses for all equipment/cards. • Annual SLA for all FOX615FOX612 equipment • Project Management resource for FOX515 upgrade project • Technical design resource for FOX515 upgrade project • Technical support for future FOX615,612 related projects • Field based installation commissioning resources for FOX515 upgrade project. • Training on FOX615/612 equipment and associated platforms • Ongoing Foxman NMS upgrades and support It is a requirement that the successful service provider will have experience in delivering a solution of similar type and scale to that being sought by ESB.

Title: Ireland – Survey services – 9231 Nationwide Tree Analysis using Lidar and Imagery
Procedure title: 9231 Nationwide Tree Analysis using Lidar and Imagery
Description: IE has a requirement for aerial drone surveys and tree analysis around our critical infrastructure assets, to include: • Visual Safety Inspections • Tree and Vegetation analyses • Fenceline analyses • Worksite Photography • Topographical Surveys/Structures Inspection • Thermal Imaging Surveys IE are seeking companies; with core expertise in imagery collection and remote sensing and who can produce on demand imaging and data that is highly accurate and comprehensive. • who can provide an end-to-end service, from data capture, processing and analysis to final reporting back to the client • with the resources in place to collate and analyse remotely sensed data recorded, proficient in the use of GIS tools and experienced with mapping, surveying, 3D modelling and tree identification and analyses • who must be a registered and in date UAS operator with IAA and have trained pilots with relevant certs of competency.
Lot description: IE has a requirement for aerial drone surveys and tree analysis around our critical infrastructure assets, to include: • Visual Safety Inspections • Tree and Vegetation analyses • Fenceline analyses • Worksite Photography • Topographical Surveys/Structures Inspection • Thermal Imaging Surveys IE are seeking companies; with core expertise in imagery collection and remote sensing and who can produce on demand imaging and data that is highly accurate and comprehensive. • who can provide an end-to-end service, from data capture, processing and analysis to final reporting back to the client • with the resources in place to collate and analyse remotely sensed data recorded, proficient in the use of GIS tools and experienced with mapping, surveying, 3D modelling and tree identification and analyses • who must be a registered and in date UAS operator with IAA and have trained pilots with relevant certs of competency.

Title: Ireland – Survey services – 9231 Nationwide Tree Analysis using Lidar and Imagery
Procedure title: 9231 Nationwide Tree Analysis using Lidar and Imagery
Description: IE has a requirement for aerial drone surveys and tree analysis around our critical infrastructure assets, to include: • Visual Safety Inspections • Tree and Vegetation analyses • Fenceline analyses • Worksite Photography • Topographical Surveys/Structures Inspection • Thermal Imaging Surveys IE are seeking companies; with core expertise in imagery collection and remote sensing and who can produce on demand imaging and data that is highly accurate and comprehensive. • who can provide an end-to-end service, from data capture, processing and analysis to final reporting back to the client • with the resources in place to collate and analyse remotely sensed data recorded, proficient in the use of GIS tools and experienced with mapping, surveying, 3D modelling and tree identification and analyses • who must be a registered and in date UAS operator with IAA and have trained pilots with relevant certs of competency.
Lot description: IE has a requirement for aerial drone surveys and tree analysis around our critical infrastructure assets, to include: • Visual Safety Inspections • Tree and Vegetation analyses • Fenceline analyses • Worksite Photography • Topographical Surveys/Structures Inspection • Thermal Imaging Surveys IE are seeking companies; with core expertise in imagery collection and remote sensing and who can produce on demand imaging and data that is highly accurate and comprehensive. • who can provide an end-to-end service, from data capture, processing and analysis to final reporting back to the client • with the resources in place to collate and analyse remotely sensed data recorded, proficient in the use of GIS tools and experienced with mapping, surveying, 3D modelling and tree identification and analyses • who must be a registered and in date UAS operator with IAA and have trained pilots with relevant certs of competency.

When a competition for a particular framework agreement or contract from the Qualification Panel is required, registered applicants may be taken through a further pre-qualification process to determine those to be invited to tender or negotiate. When determining which companies will be invited to tender, only those with a turnover of twice the annual value of the contract will be invited. Applicants who have been deemed suitably qualified may be invited to submit a formal tender for the requirements that arise during the Qualification Panel term. Description: Dublin City Council has awarded a contract to Breffni Group Ltd. The Contract comprises clearance and removal of approximately 40,000 tonnes of illegally dumped waste material and construction of boundary treatments and 117m of new 2.5m high precast boundary wall and footpath between Darndale Park and a group of Traveller Accommodation site known as the Northern Sites on the north side of Dublin within the boundaries of Darndale and Priorswood. There is a requirement for removal of hazardous waste should it be encountered. Temporary works shall include construction of a construction stage haul road through Darndale Park to provide site access and all associated reinstatement works, protection to all existing services, fencing of works areas etc. Design of temporary works shall form part of the works.

description: This is a call to competition by IE for the procurement of a Design and Build Contractor to deliver capacity enhancement works at Connolly Station, part of the DART+ Programme. DART+ is a transformative programme of projects that aims to modernise and improve existing rail services in the Greater Dublin Area (GDA). The DART network will increase from 50 kilometres to 150 kilometres transforming commuter train travel in the Greater Dublin Area. It will provide a sustainable, electrified, reliable and more frequent rail service improving capacity in all rail corridors serving Dublin, bringing DART travel with all its benefits to new and existing communities. The provision of a new electrified fleet will improve capacity and reduce greenhouse gas emissions. The successful Contractor shall develop the detailed design of the proposed alterations to Connolly Station. The Contractor shall subsequently construct the works, test and commission all systems they install and provide as-built documentation and drawings accurately detailing the works as constructed. Works will need to integrate into the existing operational station, with extensions to systems including (but not limited to) low voltage power, lighting, HVAC, CCTV, Customer Information Systems, Public Address, fire detection and suppression systems and help points.

Title: Ireland – Demolition, site preparation and clearance work – TII390_M110_Enabling Works and Specialist Heritage Works Framework for MetroLink
Procedure title: TII390_M110_Enabling Works and Specialist Heritage Works Framework for MetroLink
Description: MetroLink will provide a high speed, high capacity, high frequency, modern and efficient public transport service for passengers travelling along the Swords/Airport to City Centre corridor in Dublin, which will be capable of integration with other modes of public transport. Further information on MetroLink is available at www.metrolink.ie/ In advance of the MetroLink main infrastructure works contracts, TII will commence the procurement of the Enabling Works Programme. The Enabling Works Programme comprises the establishment of a suite of framework agreements and qualification systems select contractors to deliver enabling works which will commence in advance of the main infrastructure works contracts (in respect of civil engineering, tunnelling and station works). The enabling works will include the removal and/or relocation of existing utilities, archaeology, heritage items (for storage/replacement) and buildings from site and undertaking other survey activities. To deliver the enabling and advance works for MetroLink, TII intends to establish 3 no. multi-party framework agreements as listed below each through a negotiated procedure with a prior call for competition. • Enabling Works and Specialist Heritage Works Framework; • Utilities Framework; and • Civils Enabling Works Framework. TII also intends to establish a qualification system for independent environmental monitoring and a qualification system for archaeology services as part of the Enabling Works Programme. The proposed duration of the framework agreements is 8 years with an option to extend for 4 years to facilitate the procurement of any associated works that may be required over the duration of the Frameworks. This PIN is in connection with the Enabling Works and Specialist Heritage Works Framework. The purpose of this PIN is to alert the market to TII’s intention to undertake market consultation and subsequently commence a procurement in Q3 2025. It is anticipated that the prequalification documentation will be issued in Q3 2025 with the instructions to tenderers issued in Q4 2025 or Q1 2026. TII intends to utilise the NEC4 Engineering Construction Contract (ECC) form of contracts for call offs placed under this framework. Interested parties can register their interest at https://www.etenders.gov.ie Any interested parties wishing to respond to the market consultation in advance of procurement commencement, are required to send a request to the following email address supplychainmetrolink@tii.ie by 12:00hrs on the 23rd May 2025 seeking to be issued with a copy of the briefing pack for review and completion of the questionnaire contained within the pack. The questionnaire is required to be completed in full and returned by the closing date of the 27th May 2025 by 12:00hrs to the following email address supplychainmetrolink@tii.ie. Following receipt of completed questionnaires from interested parties, TII proposes to invite selected participants to provide further information by way of one-to-one clarification meetings to be held on the 3rd , 4th and 5th June 2025. To be deemed an interested party you must register your interest on supplychainmetrolink@tii.ie. TII intends to hold a webinar for the registered interested parties in relation to this procurement on May 29th 2025 at 12:00hrs. TII previously issued a PIN in connection with the MetroLink Advance Works packages for market consultation (reference OJ S 217/2023 10/11/2023)

integration with other modes of public transport. Further information on MetroLink is available at www.metrolink.ie MetroLink will be procured under a series of public works and services contracts: Programme Delivery Partner (“PDP”) Contract: The PDP Contract shall support Transport Infrastructure Ireland (“TII”) through providing capability and capacity to support the TII organisational structure in post-contract, construction and delivery (including contract management functions such as fulfilling role of “Project Manager” and “Supervisor” under the M401/M402 Main Civils Infrastructure Contracts and performance of the statutory function of Project Supervisor Construction Stage under the M401/M402 Main Civils Infrastructure Contracts and the M500 Contract). M401/402 Main Civils Infrastructure Contracts: Two NEC4 Engineering and Construction Contract (ECC) contracts will be let for the civil engineering and infrastructure works including track alignment preparation, stations and structures including bridges and tunnels. Further detail on the scope of the two M400 Main Civils Infrastructure Contracts is as envisaged below:  1. Southern Section M401 – Charlemont to Northwood: • Bored tunnels and portals, evacuation / intervention shafts; and • Below ground station excavations at Charlemont, St Stephen’s Green, Tara, O’Connell, Mater, Glasnevin, Griffith Park, Collins Avenue, Ballymun, Northwood up to 35m deep including shell and core structures. 2. Northern Section M402 - Northwood to Estuary: • M50 viaduct, surface route (retained cut, cut and cover) and at-grade sections; • Broadmeadow river viaduct; • Estuary Station Park and Ride Facility (bulk earthworks and site preparation); • Preparation of the Dardistown Depot site and access road; • Bored tunnels and portals, evacuation / intervention shafts; and • Stations excavations and associated logistics including Dardistown, Dublin Airport, Fosterstown, Swords Central, Seatown and Estuary. M500 Contract An availability-based design, build, finance, operate and maintain (“DBFOM”) contract to appoint a project company (“M500 Contractor”) who will carry out design and construction, raise finance in respect of such construction, and subsequently provide the integrated operation and maintenance of the public passenger transport service. The M500 Contractor will be responsible for the design, manufacture, supply and installation of the metro rolling stock, signalling system (at Grade of Operation 4 – an automated railway), a railway depot and maintenance facility, metro control centre building(s) together with the installation of all line-wide trackwork, overhead contact system, power and communication systems, mechanical and electrical systems including tunnel and station ventilation, people movement systems and the fit out and finishes in sixteen stations plus urban realm works. The M500 Contractor will be required to procure financing in respect of the abovementioned works, and following completion of the works, the M500 Contractor will be responsible for the operation and maintenance of the MetroLink system as a whole. TII proposes to award an Early Services Agreement to the preferred tenderer for the M500 Contract, pursuant to which the preferred tenderer will be required to provide early services related to, inter alia, railway systems integration prior to financial close. In advance of the award of the M400 Main Civils Infrastructure Contracts and the M500 Contract, TII intends to award a series of enabling works framework agreements (the “M100 Contracts”) and a DPS purchasing system to deliver enabling works to include the removal and/or relocation of existing utilities, archaeology, heritage items (for storage/replacement) and buildings from site and undertaking other monitoring and survey activities. Separate Periodic Notices were published for the M100 Contracts on 19th May 2025: • Civils Enabling Works Framework TED Reference: 320539-2025 - Planning • Utilities Framework TED Reference: 319450-2025 - Planning • Enabling Works and Specialist Heritage Works Framework TED Reference: 321121-2025 - Planning • Independent Monitoring and Surveying Qualification System TED Reference: 321586-2025 - Planning • Archaeology Services Qualification System TED Reference: 321984-2025 - Planning This Global PIN is further to other previous publications concerning this project including: • TED Reference: 518372-2024, released on 29 of August 2024, related to the M400 Main Civils Infrastructure Contracts. • TED Reference: 509146-2024, released on 26 August 2024, related to the PDP Contract. • TED Reference: 557522-2023, released on 15 September 2023, related to the M500 Contract. • TED Reference: 208843-2022, released on 19 April 2022, related to the M500 Contract. • TED Reference: 536230-2019, released on 12 November 2019, related to MetroLink as a whole."},"buyer-identifier":["9510201H"]}

Further information on MetroLink is available at www.metrolink.ie MetroLink will be procured under a series of public works and services contracts: Programme Delivery Partner (“PDP”) Contract: The PDP Contract shall support Transport Infrastructure Ireland (“TII”) through providing capability and capacity to support the TII organisational structure in post-contract, construction and delivery (including contract management functions such as fulfilling role of “Project Manager” and “Supervisor” under the M401/M402 Main Civils Infrastructure Contracts and performance of the statutory function of Project Supervisor Construction Stage under the M401/M402 Main Civils Infrastructure Contracts and the M500 Contract). M401/402 Main Civils Infrastructure Contracts: Two NEC4 Engineering and Construction Contract (ECC) contracts will be let for the civil engineering and infrastructure works including track alignment preparation, stations and structures including bridges and tunnels. Further detail on the scope of the two M400 Main Civils Infrastructure Contracts is as envisaged below: 1. Southern Section M401 – Charlemont to Northwood: • Bored tunnels and portals, evacuation / intervention shafts; and • Below ground station excavations at Charlemont, St Stephen’s Green, Tara, O’Connell, Mater, Glasnevin, Griffith Park, Collins Avenue, Ballymun, Northwood up to 35m deep including shell and core structures. 2. Northern Section M402 - Northwood to Estuary: • M50 viaduct, surface route (retained cut, cut and cover) and at-grade sections; • Broadmeadow river viaduct; • Estuary Station Park and Ride Facility (bulk earthworks and site preparation); • Preparation of the Dardistown Depot site and access road; • Bored tunnels and portals, evacuation / intervention shafts; and • Stations excavations and associated logistics including Dardistown, Dublin Airport, Fosterstown, Swords Central, Seatown and Estuary. M500 Contract An availability-based design, build, finance, operate and maintain (“DBFOM”) contract to appoint a project company (“M500 Contractor”) who will carry out design and construction, raise finance in respect of such construction, and subsequently provide the integrated operation and maintenance of the public passenger transport service. The M500 Contractor will be responsible for the design, manufacture, supply and installation of the metro rolling stock, signalling system (at Grade of Operation 4 – an automated railway), a railway depot and maintenance facility, metro control centre building(s) together with the installation of all line-wide trackwork, overhead contact system, power and communication systems, mechanical and electrical systems including tunnel and station ventilation, people movement systems and the fit out and finishes in sixteen stations plus urban realm works. The M500 Contractor will be required to procure financing in respect of the abovementioned works, and following completion of the works, the M500 Contractor will be responsible for the operation and maintenance of the MetroLink system as a whole. TII proposes to award an Early Services Agreement to the preferred tenderer for the M500 Contract, pursuant to which the preferred tenderer will be required to provide early services related to, inter alia, railway systems integration prior to financial close. In advance of the award of the M400 Main Civils Infrastructure Contracts and the M500 Contract, TII intends to award a series of enabling works framework agreements (the “M100 Contracts”) and a DPS purchasing system to deliver enabling works to include the removal and/or relocation of existing utilities, archaeology, heritage items (for storage/replacement) and buildings from site and undertaking other monitoring and survey activities. Separate Periodic Notices were published for the M100 Contracts on 19th May 2025: • Civils Enabling Works Framework TED Reference: 320539-2025 - Planning • Utilities Framework TED Reference: 319450-2025 - Planning • Enabling Works and Specialist Heritage Works Framework TED Reference: 321121-2025 - Planning • Independent Monitoring and Surveying Qualification System TED Reference: 321586-2025 - Planning • Archaeology Services Qualification System TED Reference: 321984-2025 - Planning This Global PIN is further to other previous publications concerning this project including: • TED Reference: 518372-2024, released on 29 of August 2024, related to the M400 Main Civils Infrastructure Contracts. • TED Reference: 509146-2024, released on 26 August 2024, related to the PDP Contract. • TED Reference: 557522-2023, released on 15 September 2023, related to the M500 Contract. • TED Reference: 208843-2022, released on 19 April 2022, related to the M500 Contract. • TED Reference: 536230-2019, released on 12 November 2019, related to MetroLink as a whole.

Procedure title: Environmental Monitoring System for the National Children's Hospital Ireland
Description: The services comprise implementation of an end-to-end Environmental Monitoring System for the new children's hospital, to be operated by Children's Health Ireland (CHI). As CHI prepares for the opening of the National Children’s Hospital Ireland (NCHI), the organisation has identified the need to develop a comprehensive Independent Environmental Monitoring system. This system will serve CHI at the NCHI and potentially the satellite facilities at CHI at Tallaght and CHI at Connolly. The system will be specifically for use in a hospital environment monitoring pharmacies, lab and speciality environments and Temperatures. The system must ensure compliance with suitable ISO accreditation standards and integrate with a centralised monitoring system that meets current environmental and temperature monitoring standards. Any contract award will be subject to funding approval.

The extent and details of these works will vary from location to location. Title: Ireland – Survey services – 9231 Nationwide Tree Analysis using Lidar and Imagery
Procedure title: 9231 Nationwide Tree Analysis using Lidar and Imagery
Description: IE has a requirement for aerial drone surveys and tree analysis around our critical infrastructure assets, to include: • Visual Safety Inspections • Tree and Vegetation analyses • Fenceline analyses • Worksite Photography • Topographical Surveys/Structures Inspection • Thermal Imaging Surveys IE are seeking companies; with core expertise in imagery collection and remote sensing and who can produce on demand imaging and data that is highly accurate and comprehensive. • who can provide an end-to-end service, from data capture, processing and analysis to final reporting back to the client • with the resources in place to collate and analyse remotely sensed data recorded, proficient in the use of GIS tools and experienced with mapping, surveying, 3D modelling and tree identification and analyses • who must be a registered and in date UAS operator with IAA and have trained pilots with relevant certs of competency.
Lot description: IE has a requirement for aerial drone surveys and tree analysis around our critical infrastructure assets, to include: • Visual Safety Inspections • Tree and Vegetation analyses • Fenceline analyses • Worksite Photography • Topographical Surveys/Structures Inspection • Thermal Imaging Surveys IE are seeking companies; with core expertise in imagery collection and remote sensing and who can produce on demand imaging and data that is highly accurate and comprehensive. • who can provide an end-to-end service, from data capture, processing and analysis to final reporting back to the client • with the resources in place to collate and analyse remotely sensed data recorded, proficient in the use of GIS tools and experienced with mapping, surveying, 3D modelling and tree identification and analyses • who must be a registered and in date UAS operator with IAA and have trained pilots with relevant certs of competency.

Title: Ireland – Construction work – 9168 Design and Build Capacity Enhancement Works at Connolly Station
Procedure title: 9168 Design and Build Capacity Enhancement Works at Connolly Station
Description: This is a call to competition by IE for the procurement of a Design and Build Contractor to deliver capacity enhancement works at Connolly Station, part of the DART+ Programme. DART+ is a transformative programme of projects that aims to modernise and improve existing rail services in the Greater Dublin Area (GDA). The DART network will increase from 50 kilometres to 150 kilometres transforming commuter train travel in the Greater Dublin Area. It will provide a sustainable, electrified, reliable and more frequent rail service improving capacity in all rail corridors serving Dublin, bringing DART travel with all its benefits to new and existing communities. The provision of a new electrified fleet will improve capacity and reduce greenhouse gas emissions. The successful Contractor shall develop the detailed design of the proposed alterations to Connolly Station. The Contractor shall subsequently construct the works, test and commission all systems they install and provide as-built documentation and drawings accurately detailing the works as constructed. Works will need to integrate into the existing operational station, with extensions to systems including (but not limited to) low voltage power, lighting, HVAC, CCTV, Customer Information Systems, Public Address, fire detection and suppression systems and help points.

Procedure title: 9165 Single Supplier Framework Agreement for Design and Build Signalling and Telecoms Contractor for DART +
Description: Iarnród Éireann (IÉ) has an existing contract in place for the Long-Term Supply, Installation, Testing, and Commissioning of a Computer-Based Interlocking System (CBIS). As part of the DART+ Programme, IÉ is seeking to appoint an experienced contractor to the DART+ Single Supplier Framework for Design & Build Signalling & Telecoms. The appointed contractor will be responsible for the design, construction, and commissioning of all Signalling and Telecoms works, with the exception of those tasks specifically designated as the responsibility of the interlocking system OEM (Original Equipment manufacturer).For the avoidance of doubt, this framework excludes interlocking system OEM works, which will continue to be delivered under IÉ’s existing CBIS Framework. The DART+ Single Supplier Framework for Design & Build Signalling & Telecoms will include the detailed design, installation, testing and commissioning (as appropriate) of the following: • A new signalling system, including lineside signals, lineside equipment housings, train detection equipment, balise installation, point operating equipment and all associated cabling. • ETCS Level 1 train protection system, designed and provided by the CBI framework supplier, will be installed and commissioned by the appointed S&T Contractor • Alterations as required where the new signalling systems will fringe to existing signalling systems. • Power supply and distribution systems to support S&T equipment, including signalling & telecoms power supply systems. • Points heating systems. • Telecoms systems (including both fibre and copper cabling) to support the signalling system. • Lineside telephones. • The decommissioning of existing level crossings, including the recovery of existing equipment. • The decommissioning and recovery of redundant signalling & telecoms systems and electrical systems. • Ancillary systems for lineside buildings and equipment housings, including lighting, cable management, telecoms connections, environmental control, fire detection and suppression systems, access control and intruder alarm systems. • Collaborating with and supporting, as required, the IÉ appointed Maintainer of the National Traffic Control Centre (NTCC), who will undertake required upgrades to systems (including the Traffic management System) within the NTCC. Similarly, the project shall interface the with existing Connolly Train Control (CTC) centre. Where any existing system is to be retained, immunisation works as required to enable the introduction of overhead Electrification (by others). • Provision of training material to support the briefing and training of drivers, signallers and other operational staff.
Lot description: This is a call to competition by IE for the procurement of a Design and Build Signalling and Telecoms Contractor by way of a single supplier Framework Agreement, one Contractor will be the sole supplier. DART+ is a transformative programme of projects that aims to modernise and improve existing rail services in the Greater Dublin Area (GDA). The DART network will increase from 50 kilometres to 150 kilometres transforming commuter train travel in the Greater Dublin Area. It will provide a sustainable, electrified, reliable and more frequent rail service improving capacity in all rail corridors serving Dublin, bringing DART travel with all its benefits to new and existing communities. The provision of a new electrified fleet will improve capacity and reduce greenhouse gas emissions.
