Éireann intends to procure low emission coaches and schools buses, and where possible zero-emission coaches with low environmental impact in compliance with the latest EURO VI Regulation. The vehicles will comply, as appropriate, with the EPA’s guidelines on road transport vehicles and the European Communities (Clean and Energy Efficient Road Transport Vehicles) (Amendment) Regulations 2021. To be considered for inclusion on a Qualification Panel(s), applicants must complete the Pre-Qualification Questionnaire (PQQ) providing relevant details in relation to the criteria set out below for assessment. It is envisaged that this qualification system will be used to either purchase and or lease during the five-year term of the Qualification System. Economic operators apply once to qualify onto the panel by providing details of their financial and technical capacity against predefined published Selection Criteria within a PQQ. The Qualification Panel for the Purchase and or Lease of Buses and Coaches will be broken down in to sub categories called Lot 1 – Purchase of Buses and Coaches Expressway, and Lot 2 – Lease of Buses and Coaches Expressway, Lot 3 - Purchase of School Buses and Coaches, Lot 4 - Lease of School Buses and Coaches, Lot 5 - Purchase of single or double deck city bus type vehicles and Lot 6 - Lease of single or double deck city bus type vehicles. Economic operators can apply for the Lot(s) that best reflect their commercial operations. Economic operators must complete a PQQ for the Lot(s) that they wish to qualify to. Only economic operators who satisfy the selection criteria of each individual Lot will qualify on to that Lot. After the initial advertisement, the panel must be advertised annually for the duration of the panel (5 years) to continually inform the market place of its existence. Economic Operators can apply to qualify on to the panel, throughout the duration of the panel. Economic Operators who are already qualified to the panel can also amend their application at any interval should their financial or technical capacity or capability change. Qualifying onto a panel does not guarantee any work and/or contracts to a supplier. There is no obligation to use the Qualification Panel and contracts can be advertised on an individual basis using the Negotiated Procedure. description: Bus Éireann intends to procure low emission coaches and schools buses, and where possible zero-emission coaches with low environmental impact in compliance with the latest EURO VI Regulation. The vehicles will comply, as appropriate, with the EPA’s guidelines on road transport vehicles and the European Communities (Clean and Energy Efficient Road Transport Vehicles) (Amendment) Regulations 2021. To be considered for inclusion on a Qualification Panel(s), applicants must complete the Pre-Qualification Questionnaire (PQQ) providing relevant details in relation to the criteria set out below for assessment. It is envisaged that this qualification system will be used to either purchase and or lease during the five-year term of the Qualification System. Economic operators apply once to qualify onto the panel by providing details of their financial and technical capacity against predefined published Selection Criteria within a PQQ. The Qualification Panel for the Purchase and or Lease of Buses and Coaches will be broken down in to sub categories called Lot 1 – Purchase of Buses and Coaches Expressway, and Lot 2 – Lease of Buses and Coaches Expressway, Lot 3 - Purchase of School Buses and Coaches, Lot 4 - Lease of School Buses and Coaches, Lot 5 - Purchase of single or double deck city bus type vehicles and Lot 6 - Lease of single or double deck city bus type vehicles. Economic operators can apply for the Lot(s) that best reflect their commercial operations. Economic operators must complete a PQQ for the Lot(s) that they wish to qualify to. Only economic operators who satisfy the selection criteria of each individual Lot will qualify on to that Lot. After the initial advertisement, the panel must be advertised annually for the duration of the panel (5 years) to continually inform the market place of its existence. Economic Operators can apply to qualify on to the panel, throughout the duration of the panel. Economic Operators who are already qualified to the panel can also amend their application at any interval should their financial or technical capacity or capability change. Title: Ireland – Buses and coaches – Annual Readvertisement of Qualification System for the Purchase and or Leasing of Buses and Coaches for Bus Éireann/Irish Bus - (Annual Readvertisement 3/8 - Amended)

Description: Bus Éireann intends to procure low emission coaches and schools buses, and where possible zero-emission coaches with low environmental impact in compliance with the latest EURO VI Regulation. The vehicles will comply, as appropriate, with the EPA’s guidelines on road transport vehicles and the European Communities (Clean and Energy Efficient Road Transport Vehicles) (Amendment) Regulations 2021. To be considered for inclusion on a Qualification Panel(s), applicants must complete the Pre-Qualification Questionnaire (PQQ) providing relevant details in relation to the criteria set out below for assessment. It is envisaged that this qualification system will be used to either purchase and or lease during the five-year term of the Qualification System. Economic operators apply once to qualify onto the panel by providing details of their financial and technical capacity against predefined published Selection Criteria within a PQQ. The Qualification Panel for the Purchase and or Lease of Buses and Coaches will be broken down in to sub categories called Lot 1 – Purchase of Buses and Coaches Expressway, and Lot 2 – Lease of Buses and Coaches Expressway, Lot 3 - Purchase of School Buses and Coaches, Lot 4 - Lease of School Buses and Coaches, Lot 5 - Purchase of single or double deck city bus type vehicles and Lot 6 - Lease of single or double deck city bus type vehicles. Economic operators can apply for the Lot(s) that best reflect their commercial operations. Economic operators must complete a PQQ for the Lot(s) that they wish to qualify to. Only economic operators who satisfy the selection criteria of each individual Lot will qualify on to that Lot. After the initial advertisement, the panel must be advertised annually for the duration of the panel (5 years) to continually inform the market place of its existence. Economic Operators can apply to qualify on to the panel, throughout the duration of the panel. Economic Operators who are already qualified to the panel can also amend their application at any interval should their financial or technical capacity or capability change. Qualifying onto a panel does not guarantee any work and/or contracts to a supplier. There is no obligation to use the Qualification Panel and contracts can be advertised on an individual basis using the Negotiated Procedure. (Annual Readvertisement 3/8 - Amended)

Title: Ireland – Education and training services – 2024/37 - Readvertisement Year 3 of Panel for suitable Service Providers for the provision of Environmental and Energy Management Training Courses and Demonstration in 2 Lots
Procedure title: 2024/37 - Readvertisement Year 3 of Panel for suitable Service Providers for the provision of Environmental and Energy Management Training Courses and Demonstration in 2 Lots
Description: LMETB established a panel from which it will source suitably qualified service providers to deliver Training programmes, from which service providers may be selected to participate in a mini competition for contract award for the design, demonstration, development ,customisation, accreditation, delivery of training programmes once specific needs arise. LMETB is advertising all its known, identified, potential programme, courses identified and run previously. This public procurement competition will be divided into Lots as described in the tender documents. Applicants may apply for one or more lots. There is no restriction to the number of Lots you can apply for provided you meet the award criteria. The Panel has been established 12th July 2024 and will run for 3 years until 11th July 2027. Applications will be accepted via email to procurement@lmetb.ie with the following subject heading: Application for Panel Membership for the provision of Environmental and Energy Management Training Courses and Demonstration in 2 Lots.

Title: Ireland – Marine construction works – 26/034 - A Qualification System for the provision of Engineering, Procurement, Construction, Operation and Maintenance Services for the Strategic Gas Emergency Reserve
Procedure title: 26/034 - A Qualification System for the provision of Engineering, Procurement, Construction, Operation and Maintenance Services for the Strategic Gas Emergency Reserve
Description: Gas Networks Ireland (GNI) is establishing a Qualification System for the provision of Engineering, Procurement, Construction (EPC) works and services (Lot 1) and Operation and Maintenance (O&M) services (Lot 2) for the Strategic Gas Emergency Reserve (SGER). Lot 1 is for the engineering, procurement, and construction works and services to complete infrastructure assets including but not limited the jetty, trestle, topside structures, pipelines, above ground installation (AGI), integration with FSRU, onshore terminal systems, related ancillary and enabling utilities to site and the management of nominated subcontractor(s). Lot 2 is for operation and maintenance services in relation to jetty, trestle, topside structures, pipelines, integration with FSRU, onshore terminal systems that may be required from time to time to facilitate the operation of the SGER. The Lot 2 contractor will be novated to the Lot 1 contractor for the duration of the EPC period, commissioning and defects correction period, with a subsequent three-year operation and maintenance period commencing from completion of commissioning. A further O&M period of up to five years is anticipated following completion of the initial period. Applicants may apply for and qualify in one or more Lots. GNI has immediate requirements which may be tendered in the near future, through an Initial Competition. Applicants who are interested in participating in the Initial Competition must submit their QSQ responses through the eTenders system by 12.00hrs (Irish time) 18th September 2026, unless amended.
Lot description: Engineering, procurement, and construction works and services to complete infrastructure assets, including but not limited to the following: • A marine jetty structure suitable to accommodate an FSRU and LNG Carrier, around 300 meters long in the Shannon Estuary at a water depth of approximately 15 - 20 meters • Marine piling • Floating Pontoon • Mooring & Breasting dolphins • Fender • Trestle • HP gas unloading, transfer hoses and connection systems • An on-shore gas receiving facility with a through put of max 121 GWh/d and a maximum operation pressure of 85 barg • Utility systems for WI correction • Metering system • Odourisation system • Venting system • Pipeline and pig traps • A high pressure gas grid connection pipeline 600mm diameter around 900m in length • A connection to the existing natural gas network • Utility connections for power, water and telecom • Integration with the FSRU • Onshore terminal systems • Pre commissioning and commissioning services and • the Management of nominated subcontractor(s) who, will be appointed for the EPC period to ensure the Lot 1 works meet the service output requirements, along with a subsequent period of three years from completion of commissioning to undertake the operation and maintenance services. Operation and maintenance services including but not limited to the following: • Jetty • Trestle • Topside structures, • Pipelines, and • Integration with FSRU and onshore terminal systems that may be required from time to time to facilitate the operation of the SGER. The Lot 2 contractor will be appointed as a nominated subcontractor to the Lot 1 contractor for the duration of the EPC period, to ensure the Lot 1 works meet service output requirements, along with a three-year operation and maintenance period commencing from completion of commissioning. A subsequent operation and maintenance period of up to five years will commence with the Lot 2 contractor following completion of the initial period. This period shall be contracted directly with the Contracting Entity.

description: Historic Mines Services comprising three lots: Lot 1 concerns monitoring (environmental, water, dust, geotechnical and geoheritage) of two historic mine sites; Lot 2 concerns Critical Failure Assessment for two tailings management facilities and Lot 3 concerns a physical risk inventory for approx. 138 historic mine sites in Ireland. Please refer to the CfT Documents area for the RFT, ESPD form and specifications for each of the three lots.
lotDescription: Lot 1 Monitoring Services: Environmental, geotechnical and geoheritage monitoring of Avoca and Silvermines. To include: • Reviews of conceptual flow model, monitoring objectives and monitoring network integrity at the sites; • Twice a year environmental monitoring including surface water, groundwater and dust; • Annual geotechnical and geoheritage monitoring. Lot 2 Critical Failure Assessment: Assess nature, effects and mitigation of dam breach at Gortmore and Shelton Abbey Tailings Management Facilities. To include: • Geotechnical review of site characterisation data • Critical Failure Assessment including: Risk assessment including credible failure scenarios; dam breach modelling and consequence classification. • Emergency preparedeness response plan (EPRP) for dam failure. • Expert Final Report & Regulatory Presentations. • Design for interim early warning system for embankment failure at Gortmore TMF. • Review of CFM and ERP after three years, or after substantive changes to the condition of the site (incidental or due to remediation works). Lot 3 Risk inventory: National inventory, risk assessment and prioritisation of physical risks at approx. 138 historic mine sites nationwide. To include: • Desk study on each site using available information. • Physical risk inspection and surveys of surface features at all sites. • Development of inventory, assessment and prioritisation scheme. • Report and GIS maps.

Title: Ireland – Technical inspection services of engineering structures – Historic Mines Services 2026
Procedure title: Historic Mines Services 2026
Description: Historic Mines Services comprising three lots: Lot 1 concerns monitoring (environmental, water, dust, geotechnical and geoheritage) of two historic mine sites; Lot 2 concerns Critical Failure Assessment for two tailings management facilities and Lot 3 concerns a physical risk inventory for approx. 138 historic mine sites in Ireland. Please refer to the CfT Documents area for the RFT, ESPD form and specifications for each of the three lots.
Lot description: Lot 1 Monitoring Services: Environmental, geotechnical and geoheritage monitoring of Avoca and Silvermines. To include: • Reviews of conceptual flow model, monitoring objectives and monitoring network integrity at the sites; • Twice a year environmental monitoring including surface water, groundwater and dust; • Annual geotechnical and geoheritage monitoring. Lot 2 Critical Failure Assessment: Assess nature, effects and mitigation of dam breach at Gortmore and Shelton Abbey Tailings Management Facilities. To include: • Geotechnical review of site characterisation data • Critical Failure Assessment including: Risk assessment including credible failure scenarios; dam breach modelling and consequence classification. • Emergency preparedeness response plan (EPRP) for dam failure. • Expert Final Report & Regulatory Presentations. • Design for interim early warning system for embankment failure at Gortmore TMF. • Review of CFM and ERP after three years, or after substantive changes to the condition of the site (incidental or due to remediation works). Lot 3 Risk inventory: National inventory, risk assessment and prioritisation of physical risks at approx. 138 historic mine sites nationwide. To include: • Desk study on each site using available information. • Physical risk inspection and surveys of surface features at all sites. • Development of inventory, assessment and prioritisation scheme. • Report and GIS maps.

Title: Ireland – IT services: consulting, software development, Internet and support – Environmental Monitoring System for the National Children's Hospital Ireland
Procedure title: Environmental Monitoring System for the National Children's Hospital Ireland
Description: The services comprise implementation of an end-to-end Environmental Monitoring System for the new children's hospital, to be operated by Children's Health Ireland (CHI). As CHI prepares for the opening of the National Children’s Hospital Ireland (NCHI), the organisation has identified the need to develop a comprehensive Independent Environmental Monitoring system. This system will serve CHI at the NCHI and potentially the satellite facilities at CHI at Tallaght and CHI at Connolly. The system will be specifically for use in a hospital environment monitoring pharmacies, lab and speciality environments and Temperatures. The system must ensure compliance with suitable ISO accreditation standards and integrate with a centralised monitoring system that meets current environmental and temperature monitoring standards. Any contract award will be subject to funding approval.

This system will serve CHI at the NCHI and potentially the satellite facilities at CHI at Tallaght and CHI at Connolly. The system will be specifically for use in a hospital environment monitoring pharmacies, lab and speciality environments and Temperatures. The system must ensure compliance with suitable ISO accreditation standards and integrate with a centralised monitoring system that meets current environmental and temperature monitoring standards. Any contract award will be subject to funding approval.

Description: The Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine (DAFM) is issuing this tender competition to enter into a contract with a vendor to supply an Area Monitoring System (AMS) Service within DAFM which has the capacity to deliver the obligations of Article 70 of Regulation 2021/2116 which requires the continued delivery of an AMS service. Article 65 of 2021/2116 defines an area monitoring system as a procedure of regular and systematic observation, tracking and assessment of agricultural activities and practices on agricultural areas by Copernicus Sentinels satellite data or other data of at least equivalent value. It is the intent of this tender competition to solicit proposals from all interested vendors possessing expertise to provide an AMS solution to accommodate the needs of the Area Monitoring and Land Systems Division, within the guidelines established in the tender documents.
Lot description: The Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine (DAFM) is issuing this tender competition to enter into a contract with a vendor to supply an Area Monitoring System (AMS) Service within DAFM which has the capacity to deliver the obligations of Article 70 of Regulation 2021/2116 which requires the continued delivery of an AMS service. Article 65 of 2021/2116 defines an area monitoring system as a procedure of regular and systematic observation, tracking and assessment of agricultural activities and practices on agricultural areas by Copernicus Sentinels satellite data or other data of at least equivalent value. It is the intent of this tender competition to solicit proposals from all interested vendors possessing expertise to provide an AMS solution to accommodate the needs of the Area Monitoring and Land Systems Division, within the guidelines established in the tender documents.

In summary, the Goods comprise: • Provision of an Ion Chromatography (IC) based solution for analysis of anions and cations • Reactive and preventative maintenance of the IC system for a 5 year duration

Description: Iarnród Éireann – Irish Rail (IÉ) is seeking to establish a contract for the design, supply, configuration, integration, commissioning, support and maintenance of a Station Services Mediation System (SSMS). The SSMS will provide the central processing, integration and management platform for real-time passenger information services across the Iarnród Éireann railway network. The system will interface with existing and future IÉ operational systems, including timetable systems, signalling systems, Passenger Information Display Systems (PIDS), Long Line Public Address (LLPA) systems and external passenger information platforms. The solution will support the phased migration from IÉ's existing Customer Information Systems to the future Centralised Traffic Control and Communications Based Interlocking (CBI) environment while maintaining continuity of passenger information services throughout the transition. The scope includes all necessary software, licences, configuration and integration services, testing, commissioning, migration, documentation, training, maintenance, technical support, cybersecurity updates, lifecycle and obsolescence management required to provide a fully operational and supported SSMS solution. The proposed contract will be for an initial period of eight (8) years, with an option for IÉ to extend the contract for a further three (3) years at its discretion.

Procedure title: Request for Tenders for the Provision of Cloud-Hosted Services and Capacity
Description: The Revenue Commissioners currently operate a large on-premise IT estate, supplemented by established Landing Zones in several Public Cloud environments. As part of an ongoing digital transformation and IT modernisation strategy, Revenue seeks to procure scalable, secure and cost-effective Cloud capacity. The tender does not commit Revenue to procure services but will provide the foundational compute, storage, networking and supplementary services required to develop, deploy and manage new digital services, as well as provide the capability to migrate existing workloads to the Cloud where considered appropriate.

Procedure title: Fire Remediation Works at Rowantree Court, Mullaghmonaghan, Monaghan
Description: The project involves the execution of fire remediation works to an existing 24-unit residential development located at Rowantree Court, Mullaghmonaghan, Monaghan, on behalf of the client, Oaklee Housing. The objective of the works is to address identified fire safety deficiencies in order to bring the building into compliance with current fire protection and life safety standards outlined in TGD Part B (Fire Safety) of the Building Regulations and other relevant codes such as IS 3218:2913 for fire alarm systems. The scope of the remediation works includes, but is not limited to: • Installation of fire-stopping systems at service penetrations and wall/floor junctions. • Replacement or upgrade of fire-rated doors, closers, and seals to comply with TGD-B. • Retrofitting of cavity barriers at floor levels in external cavity. • Fire alarm cable rerouting and improvements to service risers and shafts. • Sealing of socket/switch boxes within fire-rated partitions. • General improvement of compartmentation and passive fire protection measures. All works will be undertaken within a live residential environment, requiring a high level of coordination to minimise disruption to residents.

Procedure title: An Area Monitoring System Service
Description: The Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine (DAFM) is issuing this tender competition to enter into a contract with a vendor to supply an Area Monitoring System (AMS) Service within DAFM which has the capacity to deliver the obligations of Article 70 of Regulation 2021/2116 which requires the continued delivery of an AMS service. Article 65 of 2021/2116 defines an area monitoring system as a procedure of regular and systematic observation, tracking and assessment of agricultural activities and practices on agricultural areas by Copernicus Sentinels satellite data or other data of at least equivalent value. It is the intent of this tender competition to solicit proposals from all interested vendors possessing expertise to provide an AMS solution to accommodate the needs of the Area Monitoring and Land Systems Division, within the guidelines established in the tender documents.
Lot description: The Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine (DAFM) is issuing this tender competition to enter into a contract with a vendor to supply an Area Monitoring System (AMS) Service within DAFM which has the capacity to deliver the obligations of Article 70 of Regulation 2021/2116 which requires the continued delivery of an AMS service. Article 65 of 2021/2116 defines an area monitoring system as a procedure of regular and systematic observation, tracking and assessment of agricultural activities and practices on agricultural areas by Copernicus Sentinels satellite data or other data of at least equivalent value. It is the intent of this tender competition to solicit proposals from all interested vendors possessing expertise to provide an AMS solution to accommodate the needs of the Area Monitoring and Land Systems Division, within the guidelines established in the tender documents.

The requirement includes, but is not limited to, ignition keys, entrance door keys, luggage compartment keys, emergency access keys, security keys, service and maintenance keys, fuel access keys, and passenger facility keys. The keys supplied shall provide full functional compatibility with the associated Bus Éireann fleet vehicles, equipment, lockers, compartments, security systems, and facilities for which they are intended. The successful Supplier shall be capable of providing OEM-compatible or equivalent keys and, where required, producing keys from existing samples, key codes, or other information provided by Bus Éireann. All items shall be delivered directly to Bus Éireann depots and garages nationwide as required.

procedureTitle: The Supply of 1 X People Carrier type Vehicle
description: Kare invites you to provide a tender for the provision of the following.  1 x People Carrier Type Vehicle (e.g. Citroen Picasso or similar type) See vehicle specification Table A  The vehicle Must be able to be driven by a person holding a B class driving license.  Tenders to outline costs of vehicles inclusive of VAT and any other taxes or charges applicable to the vehicle.  Kare reserves the right to choose a supplier based on the availability of vehicles to view and purchase efficiently. All purchases are subject to the funding available Vs the costs received.  You MUST clearly specify the timelines / lead times involved with the purchase / of the vehicle outlined.  We will require evidence of the registration of the second-hand vehicle to confirm their immediate availability.  When evaluating the suitability of the vehicle, we will award scores based on the year of the vehicle, the kilometrage and the suitability for our needs. We will view the vehicle in person, to assess its suitability. We will also have the vehicle inspected by a qualified mechanic to verify the quality of the vehicle.  NOTE - All vehicles to be taxed for a minimum of 3 months upon delivery to Kare.

Title: Ireland – Motor vehicles for the transport of fewer than 10 persons – The Supply of 1 X People Carrier type Vehicle
Procedure title: The Supply of 1 X People Carrier type Vehicle
Description: Kare invites you to provide a tender for the provision of the following.  1 x People Carrier Type Vehicle (e.g. Citroen Picasso or similar type) See vehicle specification Table A  The vehicle Must be able to be driven by a person holding a B class driving license.  Tenders to outline costs of vehicles inclusive of VAT and any other taxes or charges applicable to the vehicle.  Kare reserves the right to choose a supplier based on the availability of vehicles to view and purchase efficiently. All purchases are subject to the funding available Vs the costs received.  You MUST clearly specify the timelines / lead times involved with the purchase / of the vehicle outlined.  We will require evidence of the registration of the second-hand vehicle to confirm their immediate availability.  When evaluating the suitability of the vehicle, we will award scores based on the year of the vehicle, the kilometrage and the suitability for our needs. We will view the vehicle in person, to assess its suitability. We will also have the vehicle inspected by a qualified mechanic to verify the quality of the vehicle.  NOTE - All vehicles to be taxed for a minimum of 3 months upon delivery to Kare.

Title: Ireland – Economic research services – Consultancy Services to prepare a Strategic Assessment and Preliminary Business Case for an Irish language based sports and community centre for CLG Na Gaeil Óga, Leamhcán (Lucan), Baile Átha Cliath
Procedure title: Consultancy Services to prepare a Strategic Assessment and Preliminary Business Case for an Irish language based sports and community centre for CLG Na Gaeil Óga, Leamhcán (Lucan), Baile Átha Cliath
Description: Na Gaeil Óga CLG organises more than 1,000 Irish language based events each year for participants aged 3 years and upwards. These include sports training, games, workshops, social and cultural events, Irish classes and parent and toddler activities. The club has 500 active members. At present, the club rents various facilities such as grass-based pitches, all-weather pitches, halls, gyms, ball walls and meeting rooms in Lucan and the surrounding areas to host its activities. The club’s members feel that a centrally located facility, managed by the club, would provide many advantages in terms of the development of both the club and the Irish language in the area. The club intends to engage a consultant to prepare a Strategic Assessment and Preliminary Business Case in accordance with the Infrastructure Guidelines issued by the Department of Public Expenditure, National Development Plan Delivery and Reform and as further detailed in the tender documents to support capital funding applications to various Government departments into the future. The club will be applying to An Roinn Forbartha Tuaite agus Pobail agus Gaeltachta for funding to undertake the Strategic Assessment and Preliminary Business Case.

The club’s members feel that a centrally located facility, managed by the club, would provide many advantages in terms of the development of both the club and the Irish language in the area. The club intends to engage a consultant to prepare a Strategic Assessment and Preliminary Business Case in accordance with the Infrastructure Guidelines issued by the Department of Public Expenditure, National Development Plan Delivery and Reform and as further detailed in the tender documents to support capital funding applications to various Government departments into the future. Description: The Maynooth University School of Business was established in 2007 and currently employs over 100 academic, administrative, and support staff as well as a student body of over 4,000 full time undergraduate and postgraduate students. The School of Business offers a range of undergraduate, postgraduate, and PhD programmes across a wide range of business disciplines as well as offering a suite of modules within the Arts programme. The teaching and learning experience of our students involves a series of face-to-face lectures within our state-of-the-art facilities within Maynooth’s campus delivered primarily by academic faculty but can also include guest lectures from industry. The School’s collective pedagogical strategy is further enhanced by Moodle, an online learning environment whereby learning materials, supplementary readings, case studies, or other media resources facilitating additional student engagement with individual modules. As evidence from students remains a critical element of our ongoing curriculum review procedures, we require a comprehensive student feedback solution to curate, distribute, and manage live student surveys as well as to analyse and disseminate the collected data.

Procedure title: 2026 50 The establishment of a single party FWA for a turnkey solution for a hairdressing salon including the supply delivery, installation and commissioning of Hairdressing Salon Equipment
Description: The Contracting Authority proposes to engage in a competitive process for the establishment of a single party framework agreement for a turnkey solution for a hairdressing salon including the supply delivery, installation and commissioning of Hairdressing Salon Equipment, Bespoke Furniture and associated equipment. A site visit is a compulsory part of the submission - The Contracting Authority will facilitate Site Visits to view the Contracting Authority’s premises at Drogheda Institute of Further Education, Drogheda, Co.Louth, A92 V586. Site Visits shall be organised between the 21st and 28th September 2026 between the hours of 3pm and 4pm. Tenderers wishing to make an appointment to avail of this opportunity must confirm their attendance by contacting DIFE College at dife@lmetb.ie by 18th September 2026 12 noon. Attendance at the Contracting Authority’s premises will be subject to compliance with local security and health and safety arrangements. The anticipated spend for the initial contract is in the region of €200,000 Ex.VAT

description: The Contracting Authority, Dublin City Council, intends to establish a Single Party Framework Agreement with a Integrated Design Team to deliver planning, engineering, environmental, stakeholder engagement and other specialist consultancy services for the Clontarf Flood Defence and Public Realm Project (CFDPRP). The Project is located along the Clontarf waterfront in Dublin and encompasses a highly sensitive coastal environment adjoining designated European sites, including Special Areas of Conservation (SAC) and Special Protection Areas (SPA). The Project has been initiated to address existing and future coastal and surface water flood risks while delivering a coordinated programme of public realm enhancement, active travel improvements and environmental benefits. The scheme shall be developed through an integrated design approach that balances flood resilience, climate adaptation, biodiversity, heritage, placemaking, sustainable mobility, environmental protection and stakeholder aspirations. The initial call-off contract under the Framework will require the successful Applicant to undertake all services necessary to develop the Project from commencement through option identification, scheme development, environmental assessment, statutory consent processes and detailed design. This shall include the preparation of all technical studies, surveys, modelling, assessments, reports, designs and application documentation required to secure the necessary approvals and to progress the Project to a stage suitable for procurement and construction. The Framework Agreement may subsequently be utilised by the Contracting Authority to procure additional related services, including procurement support, construction-stage services, post-consent services and other specialist consultancy services associated with the delivery of the Project. The successful Applicant shall be required to develop a fully integrated and coordinated scheme that delivers flood protection, surface water management, active travel and public realm objectives within a single coherent design solution that is environmentally sensitive, climate resilient and appropriate to the strategic importance of the Clontarf waterfront. For further information please refer to documentation available to download from www.etenders.gov.ie Resource ID 8969388 – Input when notice created . Please note that this project is subject to funding.

Procedure title: Dublin City Council Single Party Framework Agreement for an Integrated Design Team for the Clontarf Flood Defence and Public Realm Project
Description: The Contracting Authority, Dublin City Council, intends to establish a Single Party Framework Agreement with a Integrated Design Team to deliver planning, engineering, environmental, stakeholder engagement and other specialist consultancy services for the Clontarf Flood Defence and Public Realm Project (CFDPRP). The Project is located along the Clontarf waterfront in Dublin and encompasses a highly sensitive coastal environment adjoining designated European sites, including Special Areas of Conservation (SAC) and Special Protection Areas (SPA). The Project has been initiated to address existing and future coastal and surface water flood risks while delivering a coordinated programme of public realm enhancement, active travel improvements and environmental benefits. The scheme shall be developed through an integrated design approach that balances flood resilience, climate adaptation, biodiversity, heritage, placemaking, sustainable mobility, environmental protection and stakeholder aspirations. The initial call-off contract under the Framework will require the successful Applicant to undertake all services necessary to develop the Project from commencement through option identification, scheme development, environmental assessment, statutory consent processes and detailed design. This shall include the preparation of all technical studies, surveys, modelling, assessments, reports, designs and application documentation required to secure the necessary approvals and to progress the Project to a stage suitable for procurement and construction. The Framework Agreement may subsequently be utilised by the Contracting Authority to procure additional related services, including procurement support, construction-stage services, post-consent services and other specialist consultancy services associated with the delivery of the Project. The successful Applicant shall be required to develop a fully integrated and coordinated scheme that delivers flood protection, surface water management, active travel and public realm objectives within a single coherent design solution that is environmentally sensitive, climate resilient and appropriate to the strategic importance of the Clontarf waterfront. For further information please refer to documentation available to download from www.etenders.gov.ie Resource ID 8969388 – Input when notice created . Please note that this project is subject to funding.

noticeTitle: Ireland – Miscellaneous furniture and equipment – UL1063 Multi Supplier Framework for the provision of Meeting Booths to the University of Limerick
procedureTitle: UL1063 Multi Supplier Framework for the provision of Meeting Booths to the University of Limerick
description: The University of Limerick (UL) is seeking to establish a sustainable Multi-Supplier Framework Agreement for modular Acoustic Booths/Meeting Pods available in both solo and multi‑person configurations to meet the requirements of any department of UL. Requirements include: • supply of modular acoustic pods; delivery, installation and commissioning on site • integrated LED lighting, power module (e.g. 230V, RJ45, USB, USB-C) and ventilation, with optional presence/motion sensors • high‑grade acoustic panel insulation • optional internal table or worksurface • optional seating • optional mount for screen installation • stable installation Booths must be constructed using EU fire-safe materials, safety rated laminated or acoustic panels - including compliant fabrics and acoustic panels, and must offer a range of fabric/finish options to suit Library interiors. A minimum warranty period and reliable after‑sales support are required. Depending on configuration options may need to include a wheelchair‑accessible layout with suitable door width, low threshold access and appropriate internal clearances.

Procedure title: UL1063 Multi Supplier Framework for the provision of Meeting Booths to the University of Limerick
Description: The University of Limerick (UL) is seeking to establish a sustainable Multi-Supplier Framework Agreement for modular Acoustic Booths/Meeting Pods available in both solo and multi‑person configurations to meet the requirements of any department of UL. Requirements include: • supply of modular acoustic pods; delivery, installation and commissioning on site • integrated LED lighting, power module (e.g. 230V, RJ45, USB, USB-C) and ventilation, with optional presence/motion sensors • high‑grade acoustic panel insulation • optional internal table or worksurface • optional seating • optional mount for screen installation • stable installation Booths must be constructed using EU fire-safe materials, safety rated laminated or acoustic panels - including compliant fabrics and acoustic panels, and must offer a range of fabric/finish options to suit Library interiors. A minimum warranty period and reliable after‑sales support are required. Depending on configuration options may need to include a wheelchair‑accessible layout with suitable door width, low threshold access and appropriate internal clearances.

Description: Dublin City Council intends to establish a Single Party Framework Agreement with a suitably qualified service provider to deliver an initial contract for the Dublin Winter Lights Festival. The Dublin Winter Lights Festival has traditionally taken place primarily in outdoor venues and will continue to do so, while also exploring the idea of having some indoor experiences in 2027 and future years. Dublin City Council’s Dublin Winter Lights Festival has illuminated iconic landmarks and more unconventional locations previously, using a range of different projection methods, with more recent years seeing a trend towards full digital projections with locations such as the GPO, Custom House and Collins Barracks seeing full digital video mapping animations. By consistently seeking out innovative and unexpected sites, the festival has continued to evolve and stay fresh. It combines digital art, lighting design, and public performance to illuminate key cultural landmarks across the city, Note: the subject matter of this procurement relates to Title III Services as defined in Directive 2014/24/EU. Please note that this project is subject to funding. The framework agreement will be for a period of six (6) years. The Contracting Authority considers a framework term of six (6) years necessary due to the specialist nature of the services and the significant investment required by the successful Framework Member in artistic lighting infrastructure, projection equipment, storage facilities, specialist personnel, festival development and stakeholder relationships. The longer framework duration is intended to facilitate continuity of service, enable long-term planning and programming of the Dublin City Council Dublin Winter Lights Festival, support the development of artistic partnerships and innovation, and provide value for money through the amortisation of equipment and mobilisation costs over a longer period. The framework will also support the ongoing maintenance, storage and reuse of lighting infrastructure and associated equipment, contributing to sustainability objectives and reducing lifecycle costs. The duration is therefore justified by the subject matter of the framework and the need to secure consistent, high-quality delivery of a flagship cultural event and related artistic lighting projects. The Contracting Authority confirms that the period of any contracts awarded under the framework agreement may extend beyond the date of expiry of the agreement. Title: Ireland – Radioactive-, toxic-, medical- and hazardous waste services – Collection and Disposal of Category 1 Waste from Dublin Airport Passenger Terminals and Airside Stables
Procedure title: Collection and Disposal of Category 1 Waste from Dublin Airport Passenger Terminals and Airside Stables
Description: Due to the risk of introducing diseases into the European Union (EU) from third countries, there are strict rules and regulations around animal products and plants and plant products entering the EU. Any products that are prohibited from entry are seized and disposed of as Category 1 waste. Prohibited products in passengers’ luggage on airplanes poses a very particular risk to public, animal and plant health, resulting in its disposal being strictly regulated. Accordingly, there are controls are in place to ensure that seizures of prohibited food or plants at Dublin Airport is controlled and disposed of in a manner that minimises risk to public, animal and plant health. Past outbreaks of diseases (e.g. Foot and Mouth Disease) demonstrate the risks posed by products of animal origin, animal by-products (ABP) and plants being introduced to Ireland through travel. The successful tenderer will be responsible for the removal, emptying, cleaning and disinfection of the Department of Agriculture, Food and Marine bins at following locations in Dublin Airport: • Terminal One • Terminal Two • Airside Stables It must be noted the successful tenderer must be registered to land Category 1 waste under Article 23 of Regulation (EC) 1069/2009 and must be registered prior to commencing operations. The operator must also ensure to abide by all relevant requirements set out in national (SI 187 2014) and EU Legislation (Regulations 1069/2009 and 142/2011). Full details in Notice titled CN25ALander, published with the tender documents. Also please note there are Terms and Conditions from Dublin Airport Authority that the successful tenderer must comply with to operate at the airport, please refer to "Dublin Airport Authority miscellaneous charges booklet 2026" published with the tender documents.

The management of these placements is a complex, multi-stakeholder process spanning the Schools of Nursing, Applied Social Studies and Education departments, with approximately 1,750 students placed annually across a wide range of local and national settings. This activity is supported by a substantial tutor cohort - approximately 500 in Nursing, 150 in Education, and 150 in Applied Social Studies — each requiring reliable tools to oversee and assess student progress. The University is therefore inviting tenders for new software to provide an effective, efficient, and scalable platform capable of managing the full lifecycle of professional practice placements across these diverse disciplines.

The final configuration will vary depending on the final floor layouts. It is anticipated that the Plaza layout will consist of four rows of eight workstations, with the two external rows requiring rear sliding-door access and the two central rows configured back-to-back without rear access doors. Description: The objective of this tender is to implement a workforce augmentation facility where the awarded tenderer will provide additional resources to CORU to process applications for recognition and registration applications. The objective is to progress and process these applications in a timely manner. The team will be reporting directly to a Senior Manager in CORU or their designate. The supervisor and resources are to be based in Ireland so that they can attend face to face training as well as attend regular virtual team meetings.

intends to establish a multi-party framework for Port Hydrographic Survey Works, to: a. provide hydrographic, geophysical, and associated marine survey services across DPC’s operational and capital programme requirements; b. support DPC in fulfilling its statutory duties as a client in respect of health and safety coordination during the design process, across a range of civil, structural, marine, building and infrastructure projects throughout the framework term. Framework Members shall be capable of providing, as a minimum, the following survey services whether in-house or through an approved consortium: DPC requires firms with strong health and safety design coordination experience across a range of construction project types, including civil engineering, marine structures, port infrastructure, buildings, and utilities works. A. Core Survey Services Non-Exhaustive The required expertise includes, but is not limited to: • Multi-Beam EchoSounder MBES monitoring surveys of all navigation channels, berth facilities, docks, and anchorage areas; • MBES measurement surveys in association with capital and maintenance dredging works, including pre-, interim, and post-dredge surveys; • Assessment of seabed characteristic information from backscatter returns where MBES equipment is used; • Single-Beam EchoSounder SBES monitoring surveys where required, particularly at Dundalk Port and in shallow areas; • Assistance with archaeological and obstruction identification, including geophysical, magnetometer, side scan sonar SSS, and drop-down video DDV services; • Acquisition of intertidal areas and adjacent structures using LIDAR-based methods; • Establishment of new and existing berth fender lines and quay features; • Calibration and validation of port tide gauges and tide boards; • Establishment and/or validation of temporary benchmarks; • Provision of post-processing, quality control, and data management, including delivery of survey data in agreed formats XYZ, LAS, CARIS, PDF, and other formats as required; • Preparation of survey reports, cross-sections, contour plots, and comparison overlays to DPC’s requirements. • Professional indemnity, marine liability, and other insurances in the amounts required under the Framework Agreement. B. Additional Services In addition to the core survey services set out above, DPC may require Framework Members to provide the following additional services under individual call-off contracts: Additional services may include non-exhaustive: • Sub-bottom profiling surveys; • Wreck investigation and obstruction surveys; • Geotechnical sampling support positioning and data integration; • Assistance with environmental monitoring surveys suspended sediment, turbidity, etc.; • GNSS/RTK control network establishment and verification; BIM and GIS integration and delivery of survey data to DPC’s asset management systems. Candidates should note that this list is non-exhaustive, and the successful tenderer may be required to provide other survey services as requested by DPC during the Framework. Important: DPC seeks only Candidates capable of delivering all core services listed in Section 3.1A, whether in-house or through a consortium/grouping. procedureTitle: Multi-Party Framework for Port Hydrographic Survey Works
description: DPC intends to establish a multi-party framework for Port Hydrographic Survey Works, to: a. provide hydrographic, geophysical, and associated marine survey services across DPC’s operational and capital programme requirements; b. support DPC in fulfilling its statutory duties as a client in respect of health and safety coordination during the design process, across a range of civil, structural, marine, building and infrastructure projects throughout the framework term. Framework Members shall be capable of providing, as a minimum, the following survey services whether in-house or through an approved consortium: DPC requires firms with strong health and safety design coordination experience across a range of construction project types, including civil engineering, marine structures, port infrastructure, buildings, and utilities works. A. Core Survey Services Non-Exhaustive The required expertise includes, but is not limited to: • Multi-Beam EchoSounder MBES monitoring surveys of all navigation channels, berth facilities, docks, and anchorage areas; • MBES measurement surveys in association with capital and maintenance dredging works, including pre-, interim, and post-dredge surveys; • Assessment of seabed characteristic information from backscatter returns where MBES equipment is used; • Single-Beam EchoSounder SBES monitoring surveys where required, particularly at Dundalk Port and in shallow areas; • Assistance with archaeological and obstruction identification, including geophysical, magnetometer, side scan sonar SSS, and drop-down video DDV services; • Acquisition of intertidal areas and adjacent structures using LIDAR-based methods; • Establishment of new and existing berth fender lines and quay features; • Calibration and validation of port tide gauges and tide boards; • Establishment and/or validation of temporary benchmarks; • Provision of post-processing, quality control, and data management, including delivery of survey data in agreed formats XYZ, LAS, CARIS, PDF, and other formats as required; • Preparation of survey reports, cross-sections, contour plots, and comparison overlays to DPC’s requirements. • Professional indemnity, marine liability, and other insurances in the amounts required under the Framework Agreement. B. Additional Services In addition to the core survey services set out above, DPC may require Framework Members to provide the following additional services under individual call-off contracts: Additional services may include non-exhaustive: • Sub-bottom profiling surveys; • Wreck investigation and obstruction surveys; • Geotechnical sampling support positioning and data integration; • Assistance with environmental monitoring surveys suspended sediment, turbidity, etc.; • GNSS/RTK control network establishment and verification; BIM and GIS integration and delivery of survey data to DPC’s asset management systems. Candidates should note that this list is non-exhaustive, and the successful tenderer may be required to provide other survey services as requested by DPC during the Framework. Important: DPC seeks only Candidates capable of delivering all core services listed in Section 3.1A, whether in-house or through a consortium/grouping. Applications limited to one or more survey types only may be rejected.

Tipperary County Council is undertaking a competitive tendering process for the establishment of a Single-Party Framework Agreement for Architect-Led Integrated Multi-Disciplinary Consultancy Services for Public Realm, Landscape and Building Upgrade Projects in Clonmel, Co. Tipperary. The Framework Agreement will require the successful Consultant to provide, either directly or through its proposed multi-disciplinary team, all of the following services: 1. Architectural Services – Public Realm 2. Conservation Architectural Services 3. Landscape Architectural Services 4. Civil and Structural Engineering Services 5. Quantity Surveying Services 6. Project Management Services 7. Project Supervisor Design Process (PSDP) Services 8. Employer’s Representative Services 9. Public Liaison / Stakeholder Engagement Services 10. Mechanical and Electrical Engineering Services 11. Planning Services 12. Archaeological Services 13. Fire Engineering Services Only Applicants capable of providing all of the above disciplines and associated specialist expertise, whether in-house, through subcontractors or as part of a grouping/consortium, will be considered. This competition will be conducted using a restricted procedure. At Stage 1, Applicants will be assessed against the suitability and selection criteria set out in the Suitability Assessment Questionnaire. It is intended that the five highest-scoring Applicants, subject to a sufficient number meeting all minimum requirements and rules for selection, will be invited to participate in Stage 2. At Stage 2, shortlisted Applicants will be issued with the Invitation to Tender and associated tender documentation. Tenders will be evaluated in accordance with the award criteria and weightings set out in the Invitation to Tender. The highest-ranked compliant Tenderer will be appointed to the Single-Party Framework Agreement and will also be awarded the Initial Contract. The Initial Contract will relate to the further development and delivery of public realm and associated projects in Clonmel. Clonmel Town Centre requires a significant streetscape and public realm upgrade. A design previously received Part VIII approval; however, the design now requires further development, amendment and coordination to reflect the current project scope and available funding and to bring the project through detailed design, tender, construction and handover stages. Tipperary County Council has also acquired a protected structure for which design development and a Part VIII planning process will be required. The Architect-Led Design Team may therefore be required to deliver a combination of public realm, landscape, civil engineering and building upgrade works, including works to protected and heritage structures. The Architect will act as Lead Consultant and will be responsible for coordinating and managing the full multi-disciplinary design team, programme, cost and delivery of the projects. During the construction stage, the Design Team will be required to provide ongoing technical support, respond to queries arising on site and advise on proposed variations and other matters affecting the delivery of the works. Projects arising under the Framework Agreement are anticipated to be funded, in whole or in part, through the Towns and Cities Regeneration Investment Fund (TCRIF) and/or other available funding programmes. During the construction stage, the Design Team will be required to provide ongoing technical support, respond to queries arising on site and advise on proposed variations and other matters affecting the delivery of the works. Projects arising under the Framework Agreement are anticipated to be funded, in whole or in part, through the Towns and Cities Regeneration Investment Fund (TCRIF) and/or other available funding programmes. Please note that an ITT is not required for this stage of the tender process.

Description: The Contracting Authority intends to establish a single-party framework agreement for the supply of promotional merchandise for Beaumont Hospital. In the first instance, a contract of two years’ duration will be awarded for the supply of particular branded promotional merchandise. Over the course of the framework agreement, it is envisioned that the successful framework member may be required to provide alternative promotional material, depending upon need. It is anticipated that the items in question will feature the Hospital’s logo, in single colour, as set out in the Tender documents, together with a phone number, e-mail address and potentially a brief slogan.

description: Alexander Kuzminov trading as Nice Ice Cream, operating under the NOBLE brand, invites tenders for the supply, delivery, installation and commissioning of equipment for the expansion and modernisation of its artisan gelato and sorbet production facility at Unit 3, An Chistin Food Hub, Castlerea, Co. Roscommon, F45 R6F5, Ireland. The procurement comprises four lots: 1. Gelato production, fruit and berry processing, and blast freezing equipment. 2. Three professional refrigerated gelato service carts, for fixed-position operation during service. 3. Chocolate and premium ingredient processing equipment, including one melanger/refiner, an automatic tempering machine with vibrating table, a chocolate melter and a cocoa-butter incubation/crystallisation unit. 4. A modular walk-in freezer room with a normal storage setpoint of -25°C. Tenderers may tender for one, several or all lots. Each lot must be offered as a complete, independently priced supply and will be evaluated separately. One supplier may be awarded all lots if successful in each relevant evaluation and capable of delivering the combined scope. Equivalent solutions meeting the published functional and mandatory requirements are permitted. Prices must include the mandatory equipment and accessories, freight, unloading, positioning, installation and equipment-side connections within the specified scope, commissioning, operator training, conformity documentation, warranty and after-sales support in Ireland. Tenderers must clearly identify any purchaser-provided utility or building works and the boundaries of their installation responsibilities. The detailed RFT and lot schedules govern the requirements. Questions and tenders must be submitted through the appropriate eTenders facilities. The project is proposed for LEADER assistance. Contract formation and commencement are subject to funding approval, applicable grant permissions and the purchaser's written authorisation, as set out in the RFT.

Roscommon, F45 R6F5, Ireland. The procurement comprises four lots: 1. Gelato production, fruit and berry processing, and blast freezing equipment. 2. Three professional refrigerated gelato service carts, for fixed-position operation during service. 3. Chocolate and premium ingredient processing equipment, including one melanger/refiner, an automatic tempering machine with vibrating table, a chocolate melter and a cocoa-butter incubation/crystallisation unit. 4. A modular walk-in freezer room with a normal storage setpoint of -25°C. Tenderers may tender for one, several or all lots. Each lot must be offered as a complete, independently priced supply and will be evaluated separately. One supplier may be awarded all lots if successful in each relevant evaluation and capable of delivering the combined scope. Equivalent solutions meeting the published functional and mandatory requirements are permitted. Prices must include the mandatory equipment and accessories, freight, unloading, positioning, installation and equipment-side connections within the specified scope, commissioning, operator training, conformity documentation, warranty and after-sales support in Ireland. Tenderers must clearly identify any purchaser-provided utility or building works and the boundaries of their installation responsibilities. The detailed RFT and lot schedules govern the requirements. Questions and tenders must be submitted through the appropriate eTenders facilities. The project is proposed for LEADER assistance. Contract formation and commencement are subject to funding approval, applicable grant permissions and the purchaser's written authorisation, as set out in the RFT.

noticeTitle: Ireland – IT services: consulting, software development, Internet and support – TR5389 Service Provider to provide Digital workspace Monitoring Software
procedureTitle: TR5389 Service Provider to provide Digital workspace Monitoring Software
description: The Contracting Entity intends to procure a contract for a Service Provider to provide, licence, support and maintenance for ESB’s Digital workspace Monitoring Software. ESB operates the ControlUp monitoring software which enables us to leverage modern digital technologies to gather and analyse data at every critical point of our Digital Workspace infrastructure. It also provides historical data that is very important for recognising trends and proactively addressing issues. It is proposed that the Contract will include (non-exhaustive list – high level scope): ControlUp Performance Monitoring Software The supply of software support with licensing for the existing ESB Digital Workspace solution. Maintenance for all existing software. Management of software licences/subscriptions for all devices and software modules is required. Description: The Contracting Authority intends to award a contract for the supply and support of Medical Grade Fluid warmers and their corresponding consumables. The Contracting Authority requires highly reliable, safety-tested fluid warming technologies. It is a requirement that the equipment must perform accurately across a range of clinical environments and must accommodate varying clinical demands ranging from routine, low-flow continuous infusions to high-volume, rapid trauma requirements. A contract of four years’ duration shall be awarded for the provision of thirty fluid warmers, any required attachments, including all support, maintenance, repair and replacement of the equipment and the supply of all sterile single use consumables. The Contracting Authority shall remunerate the successful tenderer for the provision of the required equipment through the purchase of sterile single use consumables.

The Contracting Authority shall remunerate the successful tenderer for the provision of the required equipment through the purchase of sterile single use consumables.

Procedure title: Request for Tender for the provision of a rapid evidence review in relation to confidence in maths among children and young people in Ireland with a particular focus on girls and young women
Description: The Department is seeking research services from a suitably qualified contractor(s) to conduct a rapid evidence review in relation to confidence in mathematics among children and young people in Ireland, with a particular focus on girls and young women. For the purposes of this review, the terms children and young people and girls and young women refer to learners from the early learning and care (ELC) sector through primary and post-primary education. The review should therefore consider evidence relating to confidence in mathematics and numeracy, including learners' self-belief, mathematical self-efficacy, attitudes towards mathematics, and willingness to engage with mathematical learning across the continuum of educational provision, including key developmental and educational transition points.

Title: Ireland – Evaluation consultancy services – Request for Tenders for the Provision of Consultancy Services to Revenue (National VRT Service) in respect of the Valuation of Motor Vehicles and other Related Services
Procedure title: Request for Tenders for the Provision of Consultancy Services to Revenue (National VRT Service) in respect of the Valuation of Motor Vehicles and other Related Services
Description: Provision of Consultancy Services to Revenue (National VRT Service) in respect of the Valuation of Motor Vehicles and other Related Services. The successful Tenderer will be required to provide opinions of the Open Market Selling Price (OMSP) of motor vehicles (i.e. the price, inclusive of all taxes and duties, which motor vehicles might reasonably be expected to fetch on a first arm’s length sale thereof in this State by retail) and technical advice in respect of motor vehicles. The successful tenderer will be expected to have; Significant expertise in the valuation of motor vehicles in Ireland. Expertise in the valuation of used vehicles imported from the UK, Japan and other jurisdictions is particularly important. Specialist expertise in the full spectrum of electric, hybrid and electric hybrid vehicles. The successful Tenderer will undertake the physical examination of vehicle(s), at the request of Revenue.
Lot description: Provision of Consultancy Services to Revenue (National VRT Service) in respect of the Valuation of Motor Vehicles and other Related Services. The successful Tenderer will be required to provide opinions of the Open Market Selling Price (OMSP) of motor vehicles (i.e. the price, inclusive of all taxes and duties, which motor vehicles might reasonably be expected to fetch on a first arm’s length sale thereof in this State by retail) and technical advice in respect of motor vehicles. The successful tenderer will be expected to have; Significant expertise in the valuation of motor vehicles in Ireland. Expertise in the valuation of used vehicles imported from the UK, Japan and other jurisdictions is particularly important. Specialist expertise in the full spectrum of electric, hybrid and electric hybrid vehicles. The successful Tenderer will undertake the physical examination of vehicle(s), at the request of Revenue.

Procedure title: Single Party Framework Consultancy for the Development of a Parking Strategy for Limerick
Description: Limerick City Centre is undergoing a holistic change in the way that it manages its commuter traffic. The way in which commuters can use the road network within the city centre is being changed with the introduction of viable alternatives to the traditional car centric philosophies of the past. Enhancements through the introduction of Active travel infrastructure and future plans with respect to LSMATs and Bus connects projects will provide commuters with real viable alternatives when travelling to and from the City centre. The Mayoral program, supported by the Draft Limerick City Centre Transport Plan has the potential to enact further change in the way the city is viewed from a commuter perspective. Limerick City and County Council are aware that the proposed changes will create a number of opportunities and challenges for commuters, with one such challenge being the change to existing on street parking. It is the intention of this appointment to develop a parking strategy that will provide Limerick City and County Council a clear philosophy in the management of the existing and projected on street parking in the short, medium and long term as the projects outlined above come to fruition.

Procedure title: Garden Design for Knockreer Gardens Killarney National Park
Description: Tenders are being sought for the preparation of a Conservation Design and Development Plan (CDDP) focused on the long-term practice of conservation horticulture at Knockreer House Gardens (set out in 2.3). The Gardens are managed by the National Parks and Wildlife Service (NPWS) an Executive Agency within the Department of Housing, Local Government and Heritage. The Knockreer House Gardens are authentically unique, in that they have evolved their own character and style. Within this context, the CDDP will be guided by best international practice in conservation design and interpretation.

Procedure title: Shesknan Bridge Works
Description: The project involves the replacement/rehabilitation of a single-span road bridge in poor structural condition and has partially collapsed. Works will focus on the replacement of bridge deck and parapet walls, abutment and wingwall re-pointing, vegetation clearance, and associated ancillary works. Shesknan Bridge is a single-span masonry arch bridge of approximately 6m span, supporting a local road crossing over a natural watercourse. The bridge consists of a masonry arch barrel, stone sidewalls and parapets, with a relatively shallow depth of fill material supporting the road surface above. The recommended solution for the bridge is full replacement. This addresses advanced deterioration including reinforcement corrosion, section loss and spalling, which render repair-only strategies uneconomical and short-lived. Additional works are anticipated to include the following:  Site mobilisation and establishment.  Temporary works and access provision.  Demolition of defective components.  Parapet, abutment and wingwall works.  Vegetation clearance and habitat measures.  Road reinstatement, surfacing and safety barrier installation.  Final inspection and handover.

Procedure title: Single Party Framework Agreement for Architect Led Integrated Design Team Services for Fire Safety Remediation Works for Dublin City Council
Description: Dublin City Council proposes to engage in a competitive process to establish a single party framework agreement for architect led Integrated design team services, for Dublin City Council, to deliver the fire Safety remediation of buildings of a variety of uses under Dublin City Council ownership or partial ownership. The single party framework agreement will be established on foot of an initial contract for whole stages (Stage (i) Preliminary – Stage (v) Handover of Works) delivery of professional services in relation to the fire remediation works at a 7 storey mixed use development in Dublin City Centre, consisting of 62 residential apartments, retail units, podium car-park and approximately 3,000sqm of community facilities. For further information please refer to documentation available to download from www.etenders.gov.ie Resource ID 8836259. Please note that this project is subject to funding.

The Contracting Authority will require the successful Tenderer to have the ability to provide services they are tendering for within short notice i.e. 48 hours. The Contracting Authority will establish a single-supplier framework for the provision of the following services individually or in combination to support policing operations during special events (including VIP visits): • The provision of CCTV Services (including the provision, installation and maintenance of cameras, video links, and a video evidence management solution); • The provision of a communications vehicle (or vehicles) with equipment necessary to provide control room functionality and to support incident management); • The provision of large (outdoor) video displays; and, • The provision of a public announcement (“PA”) system (or systems). The successful Tenderer will be responsible for sourcing and providing the equipment listed above along with the provision of ancillary services and equipment necessary to provide the equipment above as a managed service.

Description: Upgrade works to the existing Cootehill Enterprise Centre, comprising thermal performance improvements and environmental upgrades to the external building envelope and façade systems. The works are divided into five separate options, each of which shall be individually priced by the Contractor and included within the Form of Tender. The five option prices shall also be combined to provide an overall tender sum. The options comprise: Option 1 – Non-Insulated Façade Upgrade: Upgrade and refurbishment of the existing external façade without the provision of additional thermal insulation, including new building signage. Option 2 – Insulated Façade Upgrade: Upgrade of the existing external façade incorporating additional thermal insulation to improve the thermal performance of the building envelope, including new building signage. Option 3 – Window and Door Replacement: Removal and replacement of the existing external windows and doors with new thermally efficient units, complete with all associated making good, flashings, sealants and finishes. Option 4 – Photovoltaic Panels: Provision and installation of a new photovoltaic (PV) panel system, including all associated supports, electrical connections, controls and ancillary works. Option 5 – Internal Wall Insulation: Provision of internal wall insulation to the identified existing external wall constructions, including all associated linings, finishes, junction treatments and making good. Tenderers shall allow for all labour, materials, plant, access, temporary works, coordination and ancillary works necessary to provide a complete installation for each option.

Procedure title: Munster Technological University (MTU) High Performance Indoor Athletics Centre (HPAC) at Bishopstown Campus, Cork.
Description: This tender relates to the Construction of a part single / part three storey High Performance Indoor Athletics Training Centre (HPAC) with associated sports laboratories, classrooms, studios and plant (approx. area 5250sqm), along with an external roof terrace, and associated landscaping, site and services works. The new facility is to be located to the south of the existing running track within the main MTU Bishopstown campus located at Rossa Avenue, Bishopstown, Cork and will be connected to the existing MTU Arena at 1st and 2nd Floor levels. Full details are in the tender documentation attached to this Contract Notice.

Description: The next phase of the State’s multi-phase approach to offshore wind delivery has seen a move to a plan-led model that will ensure ORE development and deployment is managed in a planned, strategic, and sustainable way, and enable a balanced equilibrium between achieving ORE objectives, while maintaining environmental protection, the economic well-being of local communities, and consideration of other activities taking place in our shared marine space. In turn, this will provide greater certainty for all maritime users as to where development will be situated. An important step in advancing Phase Two will be the use of forward spatial planning, and specifically the requirement to establish Offshore Renewable Energy (ORE) Designated Areas that will take place according to legislative provisions for Designated Maritime Area Plans (DMAPs) within the Maritime Area Planning (MAP) Act, 2021. This forward spatial planning will take an ecosystem-based approach, in line with EU and national policy, and will inter alia help to guide future investment and decision-making. The National DMAP will provide a spatial planning policy framework for offshore renewable energy deployment around Ireland’s coastline. The development and implementation of the National DMAP is currently underway. It will aim to designate sufficient maritime area to deliver Ireland’s ambition of having 20 GW of offshore renewable energy by 2040. Commencing with the South Coast DMAP, the State is undertaking comprehensive surveying activities through our partners in the Marine Institute (MI) and Geological Survey Ireland (GSI) or private surveyors as required to facilitate potential future offshore renewable energy development. This is taking place through a comprehensive programme of survey activity within the geographical area of each DMAP proposed and/or marine areas identified for offshore wind development within the future DMAPs, and/or marine areas identified for offshore wind development within the final DMAPs approved by the Oireachtas. In addition to the above anticipated programme of survey work, DCEE is seeking to supplement our own existing marine data with existing, high-quality, and unprocessed datasets which have been collected in recent years by private industry. This framework will focus on an all of Ireland approach (Irish Sea, Celtic Sea and Atlantic Ocean) and to potentially focus on other future DMAP areas as required. The maximum number of tenderers that can be placed on the Framework is twenty.
